title: [bug] hotkeyd's qs-overlay.sh dispatch cannot find the RDP session's embedded overlay — $mod+Tab / $mod+w open nothing on :10
description:
REPRODUCED LIVE on :10, 2026-07-29:

    $ DISPLAY=:10 qs-overlay.sh switcher
    qs-overlay: no quickshell instance for DISPLAY=:10

qs-overlay.sh's qs_target_pid() branches on the QS_RDP ENV VAR:
  QS_RDP=1 -> the overlay is embedded in the MAIN instance (no -p in cmdline)
  else     -> a separate `quickshell -p .../overlay` process
The :10 hotkeyd daemon's environ has DISPLAY=:10 and NO QS_RDP (checked
/proc/<pid>/environ). i3/config-xrdp sets QS_RDP only as the $qsenv PREFIX on
its own bindsym lines, and hotkeyd is not started from one of those. So every
overlay verb the DAEMON dispatches takes the desktop branch, looks for a
process that an RDP session deliberately does not run (qs-start.sh:133-136
skips it when QS_RDP=1), and exits 1.

WHY IT LOOKED FINE UNTIL NOW: the :10 session still had a stale separate
`-p overlay` instance from an earlier boot, so the desktop branch found
something. Restarting the session through qs-start.sh normalised it to the RDP
shape and the hole opened. The alt-tab cutover (dotfiles-hwds.40) moved the
switcher onto the daemon and inherited this dependency without noticing.

BLAST RADIUS: every daemon-dispatched overlay verb on an RDP session --
$mod+Tab, $mod+w (switcher), $mod+d (launcher), $mod+p (projects). $mod+n and
$mod+v are UNAFFECTED: qs-clip.sh / qs-notif.sh resolve the instance by
scanning for the session's quickshell rather than by trusting an env var, which
is the shape qs-overlay.sh should have.

FIX: make qs_target_pid DISCOVER instead of being told -- among this session's
quickshell pids, prefer one whose cmdline carries `-p <overlay>`, else fall
back to the main instance. Correct on both session types and independent of who
spawned the caller. Keep QS_RDP as an override if useful, but never as the sole
signal.

TEST: quickshell/test-overlay.sh already stands up a real instance; add a case
that resolves the target with QS_RDP UNSET against an RDP-shaped session (main
instance only) and asserts the verb reaches it.
close_reason:
FIXED, commit 13d6cc7. Self-verified.

qs_target_pid now DISCOVERS the host (prefer '-p <overlay>', else the session's
main instance) instead of branching on QS_RDP, which the daemon's environ never
carried. New suite quickshell/test-overlay-target.sh 6/0, all cases with QS_RDP
unset; mutation -- restoring the env-var branch turns 3 of 6 red. Regression:
test-overlay.sh 29/0, test-launcher.sh 27/0. LIVE on :10: $mod+w opens the
switcher and commits on release.

NOTE for whoever reads this later: the failure was INVISIBLE until the session
was restarted through qs-start.sh, because a stale separate overlay instance
from an earlier boot kept satisfying the desktop branch.

title: [bug] hotkeyd grab set is MONOTONIC across MappingNotify — an xrdp reconnect silently kills chords until restart, status says running
design:
USER-REPORTED, 2026-07-29, live :10 xrdp session. First as "nav mods not
working", then narrowed by the user to "direct $mod+hjkl not working, $mod+o is
correct". Both reports are the SAME defect.

=== WHAT WAS MEASURED ===

Live :10, daemon pid 3423823 (started 00:22, i.e. AFTER every cutover commit,
so its table was current -- 59 global chords, matching binds.py):

  xdotool alt+o    -> transition logged, layer=default->nav        WORKED
  xdotool alt+1    -> workspace switch fired (late, nushell start) WORKED
  xdotool alt+h/j/k/l/Left/Right/shift+h  -> nothing, 8 injections DEAD
  no BadAccess, no "i3 dispatch failed", no problem line in the log
  hotkeyd.sh status -> "running on :10"

After `hotkeyd.sh restart` on the SAME display, SAME workspace, SAME layout:

  alt+h  MOVED    alt+l  MOVED    alt+Left  MOVED    alt+Right  MOVED
  alt+z  fullscreen toggled and restored

So a subset of chords was silently unserved by a daemon reporting healthy, and
a restart was sufficient to restore them.

TWO ARTIFACTS RULED OUT, both of which faked a "DEAD" reading mid-session:
  - an injected $mod+1 landed workspace `morning-challenge` (ONE window), where
    focus left/right/up/down are legitimate no-ops. Every reading taken there is
    void; the pre-restart DEAD readings above were all taken on the 8-window
    `dotfiles` workspace, before any workspace drift.
  - alt+j / alt+k read DEAD even post-fix: that workspace is a tabbed container
    with no vertical neighbour, and bare `i3-msg focus down` no-ops identically.
    Layout, not daemon.
Also ruled out: cross-display dispatch (neither i3 moved), wrong IPC socket
(resolves to ipc-socket.2147 = the :10 i3), a stale table (59 chords = current),
i3 owning the chord (config.common no longer binds them, no panic latch in
~/.i3/config.d), and the engine itself (LayerEngine(mod='Mod1') returns
['focus left'] for a synthetic Mod1+h press).

=== ROOT CAUSE: GrabManager.on_mapping_notify (hotkeyd.py:476) ===

    r = self._resolve(chord)
    if r is None:
        self._ungrab(code, mask)
        del self._active[chord]     # <-- never re-added, by any path
        changed = True
        continue

1. THE RE-GRAB IS MONOTONIC. It iterates `self._active` -- what is STILL
   grabbed -- never the wanted chord list. The grab set can therefore only ever
   shrink. Nothing in the daemon re-derives it from the table after startup or
   a layer transition, so a chord dropped on one keymap churn is gone for the
   process lifetime.

2. THE LOSS IS SILENT. `self.problems` is cleared at line 481 (and again in
   sync_binds:449) and is printed ONLY at startup (hotkeyd.py:1185). Every
   mid-session grab failure is discarded unread. That is why the log showed
   "59 chords grabbed", zero BadAccess, and no problem line while the chords
   were already gone.

3. A REFUSED RE-GRAB IS ALSO A SILENT DROP. _grab (line 433) appends to
   problems and RETURNS before `self._active[chord] = (code, mask)`, so the
   chord is neither grabbed nor tracked -- and on_mapping_notify's `_grab` call
   at line 492 is exactly that path.

WHY XRDP TRIGGERS IT AND :0 LARGELY DOES NOT: xrdp reprograms the keymap on
every RDP (re)connect, so :10 gets MappingNotify churn that a native session
never sees. During the transient window while the keymap is being rebuilt,
keysym_to_keycode() can return 0 for keysyms that are about to exist again ->
_resolve returns None -> the chord is deleted permanently. Which chords die
depends on WHEN the notify lands, which is why the loss looks arbitrary
($mod+o survived, $mod+h did not) and why it is not reproducible on demand.

Related but distinct: dotfiles-hwds.28 (daemon survives its X server's death,
status lies) and dotfiles-hwds.29 (status cannot distinguish absent heartbeat
from stale) are the same family -- status proves LIVENESS, never SERVING. This
one needs the third thing: the grab set matching the table.

=== FIX DIRECTION ===
- on_mapping_notify must RE-SYNC AGAINST THE WANTED SET (the same chord list
  chords_for(table, current_layer) produces), not iterate the survivors. A
  keysym that is momentarily unresolvable must be retried when the keymap
  settles, not deleted.
- problems must be reported whenever they are produced, not only at startup.
  Every re-sync that ends with a non-empty problems list is a log line.
- hotkeyd.sh status should be able to answer "is the grab set the one the table
  asks for" -- a serving check, not a liveness check. Cheapest form: the daemon
  publishes grabbed-count + expected-count and status compares.

=== REGRESSION TEST (headless, no live :10 needed) ===
Drive GrabManager against a fake X whose keysym_to_keycode transiently returns
0 for one keysym, fire on_mapping_notify, let the keymap settle, fire again:
the chord MUST be grabbed again. Mutation check: today's code leaves it absent
and prints nothing.
close_reason:
FIXED in e0df62a2. on_mapping_notify and sync_binds now share one _apply() that
re-resolves the WANTED chord list (stored on sync_binds) instead of iterating
the survivors, so a chord lost to a transient keymap or refused at startup is
recovered on the next notify rather than stranded for the process lifetime.
Problems are reported when they occur, edge-triggered on message text so a
MappingNotify burst does not reprint.

EVIDENCE: 4 new tests in test_daemon.py, each mutation-verified (all 4 fail on
the pre-fix tree, all 4 pass after). pytest 341/0, test-hotkeyd.sh 107/0,
test-panic.sh 54/0, test-nav-mode.sh 40/0 both mod shapes. Live on :10 after
restarting the daemon on the fixed code: alt+h / alt+l / alt+Right all move
focus again.

FOLLOW-UP FILED SEPARATELY: hotkeyd.sh status still reports LIVENESS only -- it
said "running" through the entire outage. A serving check (grabbed count vs
table-expected count) is the remaining half and belongs with dotfiles-hwds.28 /
.29, not here.

title: hotkeyd closes quickshell overlays — $mod+n and $mod+v dismiss themselves after ~3s
design:
USER-REPORTED, reproduced and root-caused, 2026-07-28. $mod+n (notifications)
and $mod+v (clipboard picker) "seem not working" while $mod+w still works.

NOT a bind problem. i3's binds fire correctly -- subscribing to i3 binding
events while injecting shows symbol=n -> exec qs-notif.sh and symbol=v -> exec
qs-clip.sh, both dispatched. The scripts run clean standalone (rc 0). The
picker WINDOW opens: i3's tree goes 7 -> 8 windows.

THE PICKER THEN CLOSES ITSELF after ~3 seconds. Timed:

    t=0     7 windows
    t=+0.3  8   <- picker mapped
    t=+1    8
    t=+2    8
    t=+4    7   <- gone, nobody asked
    t=+7    7

HOTKEYD IS THE CAUSE. Controlled experiment, same display, same script:

    daemon RUNNING  -> picker gone by t=+4s
    daemon STOPPED  -> picker still open at t=+6s   (8 windows throughout)

Stopping the daemon is sufficient to fix it; starting it reintroduces it.

WHY $mod+w IS UNAFFECTED, which is the clue to the mechanism: the task switcher
is driven by quickshell/qs-keymon.py reading raw XI2 events, and i3 holds only a
`nop` grab to stop the key leaking. It never opens an overlay window. $mod+n and
$mod+v both open a quickshell overlay that takes focus and (per qs-clip.sh's
header) a keyboard grab. So the failure is specific to overlays that grab.

LIKELY MECHANISM, unproven: the overlay takes an active keyboard grab when it
opens; hotkeyd's XI2 passive grabs interact with that -- either the overlay's
grab fails and it dismisses itself, or hotkeyd's grab set is re-synced (it
re-grabs on layer transitions and on XI_HIERARCHY_CHANGED / XI_DEVICE_CHANGED)
and that disturbs the overlay's grab or its focus. The ~3s delay is suspicious
and worth measuring against the daemon's own timers -- it is close to nothing in
hotkeyd's known intervals (0.25s idle select, 1s heartbeat, 120ms release
guard), so the delay may belong to the overlay's own dismiss-on-focus-loss.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is a REGRESSION IN DAILY USE introduced by arming autostart
(a76e9a9). Every suite is green; the nav cutover works; and two everyday
features silently broke. It was found only because the user tried to use their
own machine.

FIRST DIAGNOSTIC STEP: run the overlay with hotkeyd running and capture whether
its XGrabKeyboard succeeds or returns AlreadyGrabbed / is broken by a subsequent
hotkeyd re-grab. hotkeyd's transition log (dotfiles-hwds.27, merged) now records
every grab re-sync, so correlate the picker's dismiss timestamp against it.

ALSO CHECK against dotfiles-hwds.30: :0 has a STUCK exclusive keyboard grab
whose holder was never identified, and quickshell was ruled out there only by a
restart. If hotkeyd disturbs overlay grabs, the two may be the same underlying
interaction seen from opposite ends -- one where the overlay dies, one where its
grab outlives it.

WORKAROUND for the user meanwhile: `hotkeyd.sh stop :10` restores $mod+n and
$mod+v (and loses nav). $mod+Shift+r (panic) does the same and also hands nav
back to i3, which is the better trade.
notes:
LIVE VERIFIED after landing, on the real xrdp :10 session with the daemon running (pid 3828280), 2026-07-29.

ORACLE MATTERS HERE: 'xdotool search --name ^qs-clip$' matches the window
OBJECT quickshell keeps alive while the picker is HIDDEN, so it reports the
picker up forever and every assertion passes vacuously. My first live run used
it and was worthless. The shipped suite is right: --onlyvisible. Re-run with a
baseline assertion (picker_up must be False before the chord) so a vacuous pass
cannot hide.

$mod+v (alt+v on :10, still an i3 bind -- overlay group not cut over yet):
  baseline            picker_up=False
  t=+1.5s after chord True
  t=+1.2s alt HELD    True
  t=+2.5s alt HELD    True
  t=+4s after release True
  after toggle        False
$mod+n: identical shape, PASS.

The pre-fix failure was dismissal ~3s after opening while $mod was held; the
2.5s hold is that window and nothing dismissed.

SESSION STATE FOUND AND CORRECTED: the box was PANICKED (fallback linked at
~/.i3/config.d/zz-fallback-binds.conf, no daemon). 'hotkeyd-panic.sh resume'
unlinked the fallback and reloaded i3 on BOTH :0 and :10, but started the daemon
only on :10 -- so :0 was left with neither the daemon nor the fallback, i.e.
every migrated group (workspace, layout, directional, screenshot, alt-tab,
system) dead on the native display. Started :0 by hand; both now report
serving (:0 pid 3832231, :10 pid 3828280, --health clean on :0).
close_reason:
AUDITED: APPROVED (reviewer re-verified, not taking implementer numbers on trust)

Branch bd-dotfiles-hwds.31.0, single commit 5a6835eb, 5 files +825/-16.
Pre-flight: git log main..branch non-empty (1 commit). Worktree clean.

CONTRACT (bug report, no formal criteria) — the picker must survive a held
passive grab and still close on a real focus change:
- quickshell/test-overlay-grab.sh on the branch: 25 passed, 0 failed (re-run by
  the reviewer on a sandboxed Xvfb+i3, not the live session).
- PHASE 1 pins the reported bug directly: 'clip picker survives a 2.5s held
  passive grab' green.
- PHASE 2 pins the inverse: 'a real focus change still closes it' green, both
  overlays.

MUTATION, run by the reviewer (the implementer's numbers reproduced):
- fail-open mutant (exitCode!=0 branch hides anyway, ClipHistory only):
  23 passed, 2 failed — both failures in PHASE 1.5 clip, NotifHistory phases
  stayed green, so the phases are disjoint as claimed.
- pre-fix mutant (restore root.hide() straight off active===false in
  ClipHistory): PHASE 1 clip goes RED ('still up while the grabbed key is
  held', expected 1 actual 0). The suite would have caught the original
  regression.

REGRESSIONS:
- quickshell/test-clip-history.sh  87 passed 0 failed (matches main baseline)
- pytest hotkeyd i3 quickshell/test_qs_region_geometry.py  322 passed
- quickshell/test-notif-history.sh  126 passed 1 FAILED — but MAIN IS 126/1 TOO,
  identical count, so this is NOT from this branch. The live failure on main is
  'reload-restarts-the-bar: $mod+Shift+c chains a qs-start exec onto the
  reload' — i3/config:81 now reads 'bindsym $mod+Shift+c restart' after the
  restart-verb consolidation (28ceeffc), and the assertion was never updated.
  Filed separately. NOT gated on in the post-merge command for exactly this
  reason (it is red on base).

DEVIATIONS: implementer logged the rebase hazard (main reverted b1ed44ed but
keeps it as an ancestor, so a plain rebase silently drops the fix) and rebuilt
the branch as reset --hard main + revert-the-revert + re-apply. Verified: the
branch's diff vs main is ONLY the grab fix — sxg1's normalization is not
duplicated, it is already on main via c0269a5a.

Code read in full, not just the diff. Fail-open direction is correct and
documented at both call sites: exit 0 = known, 1 = cannot tell, hide only on
0-and-different. No TODO/FIXME/stub markers in any of the 5 files.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED, none blocking (see discovered issues).

title: [bug] ModeBar's unknown-mode fallback renders the pill as 'system' — the switcher layer reads as the poweroff mode
description:
USER-REPORTED on the live :10 bar, 2026-07-29 ('why mod+w making window frame? new mode is there, in the bar').

REPRODUCED: with the alt-tab switcher layer up the bar's mode strip paints

    [system] switcher

i3's workspaces are untouched (get_workspaces still dotfiles/morning-challenge) -- the mode strip simply replaces the workspace strip while a mode is up, which is by design.

TWO SEPARATE FALLBACKS COMBINE INTO A LIE, quickshell/config/Common/ModeBarTheme.qml:
- displayName() (line 129) ends its ternary chain with a hardcoded ': "system"', so EVERY unrecognised mode gets the pill label 'system'.
- resolve() (line 96) returns "" for an unknown mode, and hintsFor() then renders [{text: mode, key: ""}] -- the raw layer name with no key.

So the pill says 'system' and the hint says 'switcher'.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC NIT: 'system' is a REAL mode carrying reboot/poweroff/hibernate on single letters (LAYERS['system'], $mod+0). A user who trusts the pill and types 'p' expecting the switcher's behaviour gets a shutdown. The catch-all makes an unknown layer indistinguishable from the most destructive one.

INTRODUCED BY dotfiles-hwds.40 (alt-tab cutover): the switcher layer publishes on the state socket like every other layer, but got no ft009 registry entry. Any future layer hits the same trap silently -- the failure mode is a wrong label, not a blank one, so nothing looks broken.

FIX: register 'switcher' (resolve + displayName + a hints row: Tab next, Shift+Tab prev, space search, Enter confirm, Esc cancel, commit on $mod release), and make the unknown-mode pill fall back to the RAW MODE NAME rather than 'system' -- keep the indexOf('(l)ock') arm, which is what the long i3 label string needs.
close_reason:
FIXED, commit 72624e4. Self-verified (implementer == reviewer this session).

Root cause was TWO fallbacks combining: displayName()'s hardcoded ': "system"'
tail painted any unrecognised mode with the SYSTEM mode's pill, while resolve()
returned "" so the hint strip echoed the raw name -> '[system] switcher'.
qs-focus-border separately coloured the ring for ANY non-default layer.

Fix: a layer can be SILENT (ModeBarTheme.silentModes + silent();
qs-focus-border SILENT_LAYERS + layer_colours_ring). Rendering decision only --
the daemon still publishes layer=switcher. Opt-IN: an unclassified layer still
warns. Bar.qml folds silence into currentMode, not just ModeBar, because the
workspace row / ticker / tray are gated on it too.
displayName now derives from resolve so the two cannot drift apart again.

EVIDENCE: test-mode-bar.sh 111/0 (was 105); mutation -- reverting ModeBar's
silence guard turns switcher-silent.visible red alone. test_qs_focus_border_
mode.py new block green; its 8 pre-existing failures are dotfiles-5quz, red on
base, count unchanged. LIVE on :10 with $mod held: overlay up, workspaces
still painted, no pill, no red ring, commit on release.

title: Overlay group cutover: $mod+n and $mod+v leave i3
design:
The last two everyday chords still owned by i3 move to hotkeyd/binds.py:

  bindsym $mod+n exec --no-startup-id ~/.dotfiles/quickshell/qs-notif.sh toggle   (i3/config.common:25)
  bindsym $mod+v exec --no-startup-id ~/.dotfiles/quickshell/qs-clip.sh toggle    (i3/config.common:92)

WHY THIS WAS BLOCKED UNTIL NOW: dotfiles-hwds.31. A daemon holding a passive
grab on a HELD key makes X send FocusOut(mode=NotifyGrab) to the focused
window; Qt reported the overlay deactivated and it dismissed itself ~3s after
opening. Migrating these two while that was live would have made it WORSE, not
equal -- once the daemon owns $mod+v, the grab that causes the FocusOut is held
by the very keystroke that opens the picker. hwds.31 landed (671dd1bb) and was
live-verified on :10.

THE SHARP EDGE THIS CUTOVER MUST PROVE, and the reason it is not a copy of the
screenshot group: with i3 owning the chord the overlay opened and only LATER met
a held $mod. With hotkeyd owning it, the overlay opens WHILE $mod is down and
the daemon's grab is active -- so it races the everActive guard, which only arms
the blur probe once the window has actually held focus. If the window is mapped
during the grab and never sees a real focus-in, everActive stays false and
nothing hides it (safe), but the picker may also never take keyboard focus,
which would make it unusable rather than self-dismissing. MEASURE BOTH: a quick
tap AND a 3s hold of $mod+v / $mod+n, asserting the overlay is visible AND
focused (_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW), not merely mapped.

ORACLE WARNING, learned the hard way in the hwds.31 audit: 'xdotool search
--name ^qs-clip$' matches the window OBJECT quickshell keeps alive while the
overlay is HIDDEN, so it reports the picker up forever and every assertion
passes vacuously. Use --onlyvisible, and assert a False baseline first.
acceptance_criteria:
1. hotkeyd/binds.py carries both chords; i3/config.common carries neither (a comment pointer stays, per the screenshot/layout cutover convention).
2. i3/config.d/zz-fallback-binds.conf gains both, so hotkeyd-panic.sh panic still restores them. Pinned by test_the_fallback_is_exactly_what_binds_py_owns_and_i3_does_not under BOTH $mod resolutions (Mod4 and Mod1).
3. quickshell/test-notif-history.sh PHASE 3 (n-is-notif-toggle, ~line 1004) asserts the exact i3 bindsym line for $mod+n on both entry points. Re-point it at the daemon's table the way test-nav-mode.sh was re-pointed (21fddab2); do NOT delete the coverage.
4. Grab count rises by 2 on both displays; zero BadAccess.
5. Suites green: pytest, test-hotkeyd.sh, test-panic.sh, test-clip-history.sh, test-overlay-grab.sh. test-notif-history.sh has ONE pre-existing failure on base (dotfiles-ph03, $mod+Shift+c) -- the count must not grow.
6. i3 -C clean on the normal tree AND the panic-linked tree.
7. LIVE on :10 in the correct order (i3-msg reload THEN daemon restart -- the reverse leaves both engines owning the chord and double-fires with no BadAccess to warn you): tap $mod+v -> exactly one picker, visible AND focused; hold $mod+v 3s -> still visible and focused after release. Same for $mod+n.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED, commit 168ace2 on main.

FILES: hotkeyd/binds.py (+the group), i3/config.common (-2 binds, comment
pointers), i3/config-xrdp (+2, proot keeps them), zz-fallback-binds.conf (+2),
hotkeyd/test_daemon.py (stub keymap n=57 v=55), quickshell/test-notif-history.sh
(PHASE 3 re-pointed at the daemon).

RED FIRST, both steps:
- adding the binds while i3 still had them ->
  test_no_chord_is_owned_by_both_i3_and_the_daemon FAILED under Mod4 AND Mod1,
  naming (('Mod1',),'n') and (('Mod1',),'v').
- removing them from i3 before touching the fallback ->
  test_the_fallback_is_exactly_what_binds_py_owns_and_i3_does_not FAILED under
  both resolutions, 'Extra items in the right set: v, n'.
Both green after the corresponding edit.

CRITERIA:
1. binds.py has both, config.common has neither. Comment pointers per the
   screenshot/layout convention.
2. fallback has both; the exact-set test passes under Mod4 and Mod1.
3. test-notif-history.sh PHASE 3 re-pointed, not deleted -- it now pins that
   the two entry points DIFFER (config-xrdp keeps the i3 line, i3/config does
   not, binds.py carries the chord, the fallback carries the i3 spelling).
4. 65 -> 67 grabs on BOTH displays (hotkeyd-10.log, hotkeyd-0.log). No
   BadAccess, no grab problems logged.
5. pytest 399/0, test-hotkeyd.sh 132/0, test-panic.sh 54/0, test-launcher.sh
   27/0, test-nav-mode.sh both shapes, test-clip-history.sh 87/0,
   test-overlay-grab.sh 25/0. test-notif-history.sh 127/1 -- the 1 is
   dotfiles-ph03, red on base, count did not grow.
6. i3 -C clean on i3/config and i3/config-xrdp.
7. LIVE on :10, after i3-msg reload THEN daemon restart (both displays):
     qs-clip  TAP  1 window, _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW='qs-clip'
     qs-clip  HOLD 1 window + focused at t=+1.5s and t=+3.1s with $mod DOWN,
              still 1 + focused 3s after release, closes on demand
     qs-notif identical shape
   Focus asserted, not just visibility. Oracle is --onlyvisible with a False
   baseline first (bare 'xdotool search' matches the hidden window object and
   passes vacuously -- the trap from the hwds.31 audit).

SCOPE DECISION worth reviewing: config-xrdp restating both binds is NOT what
dotfiles-hwds.39 did for the screenshot group, which is why dotfiles-3qd exists.
Chose to not repeat that regression rather than file a second copy of it.

DISCOVERED: dotfiles-gppv (P3) -- session_key_of's 2>/dev/null is ordered after
the redirect, so an unreadable /proc/PID/environ prints to the user's terminal
on every toggle. Seen live during this verification, in both scripts.
close_reason:
SELF-VERIFIED AND CLOSED, commit 168ace2. NO INDEPENDENT AUDIT — implementer and reviewer are the same session here, so read the evidence rather than the verdict.

All 7 acceptance criteria met; full measurements in the notes above. Highlights:
- RED observed before each fix (double-ownership under both $mod resolutions,
  then fallback drift under both) — the tests are not vacuous.
- 65 -> 67 grabs on :0 AND :10, no BadAccess.
- Live on :10: tap and 3s hold of both chords, each leaving exactly one window
  mapped and _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW pointing at it, during the hold and after
  release.
- Suites green; test-notif-history.sh's single failure is dotfiles-ph03, red on
  base, count unchanged.

ONE SCOPE DECISION taken without asking, flagged for review: i3/config-xrdp
restates both binds so the proot Arch / Termux:X11 session keeps them.
dotfiles-hwds.39 did NOT do this for the screenshot group, and dotfiles-3qd is
the resulting complaint. If the intended policy is that proot loses binds as
they migrate, revert that hunk of config-xrdp.

title: sp020 T15: alt-tab cutover — $mod+Tab / $mod+w become a hotkeyd hold-layer, qs-keymon.py retires
design:
THE GROUP: $mod+Tab and $mod+w (currently `nop` grabs in i3/config.d/native.conf
lines 129-132 as Mod4+/Mod1+ pairs, and wsl.conf lines 13-14 as $mod+ forms).
Both today do nothing in i3 -- the grab exists only to stop the key leaking to
the focused app while quickshell/qs-keymon.py reads raw XI2 events and drives
the switcher. Two event mechanisms for one feature; sp020 exists to end that.

WHY THIS IS THE MARQUEE CASE. The switcher needs state carried between a press
and a release -- cycle on repeated Tab while $mod stays down, commit on $mod
release. i3 cannot express it at all. hotkeyd can, and the engine pieces already
exist: Layer.mods declares a held-modifier sublayer, and hotkeyd.layer_chords
grabs the modifier KEYSYMS themselves (MOD_KEYSYMS_BY_NAME) while the layer is
up, which is exactly how nav sees Ctrl/Alt.

SHAPE: a `switcher` layer entered by $mod+Tab / $mod+w, driven entirely over
the IPC verbs qs-overlay.sh ALREADY exposes -- no new quickshell entry points:
    switcher          -> qs_call switcher next
    switcher-prev     -> qs_call switcher prev
    switcher-search   -> qs_call switcher search
    switcher-confirm  -> qs_call switcher confirm
    switcher-cancel   -> qs_call switcher cancel
Layer binds: Tab/w -> next, ISO_Left_Tab (Shift+Tab) -> prev, space -> search,
Escape -> cancel + exit. Commit fires on $mod RELEASE and exits the layer.

ENGINE FEATURE REQUIRED (this is the real work, not the table):
`Layer` needs a hold-modifier that ENDS the layer with an action. Today
layers.handle returns [] for every modifier event -- "modifiers never act on
their own" (layers.py:335) -- and layers exit only via exit_keys or one_shot.
Add a declared hold modifier whose RELEASE dispatches an action and exits.

THREE MEASURED HAZARDS, each needing a test, not an assumption:

1. $mod as a sublayer name. Layer.mods keys canonicalize through
   B.MODIFIER_ALIASES (layers._active_mod), which has no "$mod" entry -> resolves
   None. The hold modifier must resolve per display like chords do, or the
   feature works on :0 and is dead on :10.

2. The engine never SAW the $mod press. Super_L is not grabbed in the default
   layer, so at layer-entry time _held is empty, and reconcile_holds is
   RETRACT-ONLY by design (layers.py:243) -- it will not assert a hold from the
   event mask. So commit must fire on OBSERVING the hold modifier's release
   while the layer is up, never on "we believed it was held".

3. RELEASE-BEFORE-GRAB RACE. A fast $mod+Tab tap can release $mod before the
   layer's grabs are installed; the release is then never delivered, the layer
   stays up and the switcher hangs open with nothing held. Needs a bounded
   fallback (exit_keys Escape/Return are the floor; consider corroborating
   against the event mask on the next key). A hung switcher that eats the
   keyboard is the failure mode this task must not ship.

RETIREMENT: quickshell/qs-keymon.py is DELETED and Overlay.qml's keyMonitor
Process + its modHeld/shiftHeld tracking (Overlay.qml:224-281) goes with it.
Note before deleting: keymon also emits mouse btnpress/btnrelease, which NO
consumer reads -- Overlay.qml's handler drops them through every branch. Dead
weight, confirmed by grep, not carried over. The sway path (Keys.onReleased,
Overlay.qml:588+) is untouched: it is Wayland and this daemon is X11-only.

XRDP :10 EXPOSURE: xrdp synthesizes Shift around every character (sp020), so
Shift+Tab -> prev is the least trustworthy bind in the group on that display,
and dotfiles-hwds.24 (release-press-release) bears directly on a feature whose
whole contract is a release. Live-verify on :10 from a REAL RDP client.

DEPENDS: none hard. NOT blocked by dotfiles-hwds.31 (daemon closes grabbing
overlays) -- that bug spares $mod+w today precisely because the switcher overlay
takes no keyboard grab, which is what makes it safe to migrate first. Confirm
that still holds before cutover.

ACCEPTANCE
- $mod+Tab cycles, $mod release commits, on :0 and :10
- qs-keymon.py gone; no reference in quickshell/ or i3/
- ownership map clean under both mod resolutions; zero BadAccess
- a released-before-grab tap cannot leave the layer up
notes:
GAP 2 CLOSED (user overrode my recommendation to keep the sweep). Commit cd230c47, stacked on d6454d97 — d6454d97 left intact, not amended.

WHAT CHANGED: quickshell/qs-start.sh no longer runs qs_kill_session -f 'qs-keymon.py'.
That was the LAST live reference to the deleted file anywhere under quickshell/ or
i3/, so the criterion 'no reference in quickshell/ or i3/' is now met literally, not
by argument. Verified: grep -rn 'qs-keymon' quickshell/ i3/ returns 11 hits, ALL of
them comments/prose explaining the migration; zero code.

THE HAZARD THE SWEEP WAS COVERING IS NOT GONE, it is now written down instead of
paid for on every bar restart. A machine whose quickshell has not been restarted
since this landed still has the old process's DETACHED listener alive, and it drives
the switcher alongside the daemon — every Tab cycles twice. Restarting quickshell
does NOT reap it (precisely why the sweep existed). The remedy is recorded at the
removal site in qs-start.sh: 'pkill -f qs-keymon.py' once, or any logout/reboot.
ONE-TIME, PER MACHINE. Worth doing before judging the switcher's live behaviour —

qs-keymon.py and was never this cutover's to remove.

  python3 -m pytest hotkeyd/ -q       -> 399 passed
  bash quickshell/test-overlay.sh     -> 29 passed, 0 failed

                                      -> 51 passed, 1 failed

(test-notif-daemon.sh:649) expects 1 occurrence of QS_NOTIF_FILE in Bar.qml and
counts 2 — because the second is a COMMENT at Bar.qml:285, not code. Production code
is correct; the grep-count assertion is. Filed as dotfiles-3vfq (P3) with the three
fix options and the observation that the whole a3 grep-count block at :641-652 shares
the defect — it cannot tell 'Bar.qml reads the file' from 'Bar.qml mentions the
string'.

STATUS UNCHANGED: still in_progress. The close gate is not the implementer's.
close_reason:
AUDITED: APPROVED (user-directed close; the audit itself was run by the implementer via work-audit — recorded as such, not as an independent gate).

CRITERIA VERIFIED
- '$mod+Tab cycles, $mod release commits, on :0 and :10' — MECHANISM verified on a
  real X server; the ATTENDED half is explicitly NOT run (see CARRIED FORWARD).
  live_check.py stage 5f drives the real Daemon on a real display end to end:

- 'a released-before-grab tap cannot leave the layer up' — live_check 5f reproduces
  the race rather than simulating it: the $mod release is injected for real,
  sw_pump() returns [], the layer is asserted STILL UP on events alone, and the

MUTATION-PROVEN, which is what a self-audit can offer in place of independence.
9 unit mutants, ALL KILLED against a 399-passed baseline: keysym_for reverted to
code-only (2 failed); SHIFTED_KEYSYM filter removed (2); hold-masked grabs removed
(2); reconcile_mods short-circuit reverted (2); canon_modifier stops resolving $mod
(28); xkb/xf86 keysym groups unloaded (2); fallback loses $mod+w (2); hold release
exits without dispatching (7); grab dedupe removed (1).
Plus 1 LIVE mutant, killed: neutering reconcile_hold_layer drops test-hotkeyd.sh
from 132/0 to 126 passed / 6 failed, and the failures are exactly the race
assertions — including 'the layer's bare keys went back to applications with it'
listing Tab and q still grabbed, which IS the hung-switcher failure the task said

TESTS: 399 pytest (all pass), 132 runtime assertions in test-hotkeyd.sh (0 failed;
was 107 pre-task, +25 from the new live stage), 40 in i3/test-nav-mode.sh across
both mod shapes, 29 in quickshell/test-overlay.sh. One failure in
test-notif-daemon.sh (51/1) is PRE-EXISTING ON MAIN and proven not mine —
Bar.qml is untouched by this branch and main carries the identical count; filed as
dotfiles-3vfq.

DEVIATIONS: three, all logged during work rather than discovered at audit.
1. The task's stated mechanism was WRONG and this was measured, not argued: a
   passive grab installed on an already-held key never activates, so the

title: sp020: screenshot-group cutover — Print / $mod+Print / $mod+Shift+Print / $mod+Shift+s leave i3 for hotkeyd
design:
SCOPE (grab-ownership closure over BOTH $mod resolutions, Mod4 on :0 / Mod1 on :10):

  Print                        exec i3-scrot            (bare, no modifier)
  $mod+Print       --release   exec i3-scrot -w
  $mod+Shift+Print --release   exec i3-scrot -s
  $mod+Shift+s                 exec quickshell/qs-screenshot.sh

All four live in i3/config.common (lines 93-95, 146). No other chord in the
repo touches Print or the s keysym under those masks, so the closure is these
four and nothing widens it.

WHAT STAYS IN i3, deliberately:
  mode "screenshot" / mode "screenshot-drag" (config.common:123,142). These are
  NOT keybind groups -- qs-screenshot.sh / qs-region.py enter them via i3-msg
  purely so Bar.qml paints its hint strip, and their only bindsyms (Escape / q)
  are dead-overlay fallbacks that fire when the selector's own grab is gone.
  Migrating them would mean the daemon holding grabs on bare Escape/q for the
  life of a screenshot -- the dotfiles-ux1 trap. They stay.

  Consequence to VERIFY, not assume: layers.LayerEngine refuses layer entry
  while i3 is in a non-default mode (_i3_owns_the_keyboard). The screenshot
  modes therefore suppress nav entry while a capture is in flight. That is the
  correct arbitration, but assert it rather than infer it.

RELEASE SEMANTICS. Two of the four are --release binds; Bind(on_release=True)
already models this and the engine matches it (layers._match). Known exposure:
dotfiles-hwds.24 (OPEN, P1) -- xrdp :10 delivers each character as
release-press-release, which may double-fire on_release binds. i3's own
--release binds have carried the identical exposure since before the daemon, so
this cutover does not create the risk, but the live matrix must exercise
$mod+Print on :10 from a REAL RDP client (not XTEST) and count the i3-scrot
invocations. If it double-fires, that is hwds.24's evidence, filed there.

BARE Print. First global bind in the table with NO modifier at all. Confirm the
grab set handles a zero-mask chord with its lock-bit variants (Mod2/Lock) --
the daemon builds those from the base mask, and a bare key's base mask is 0.

CUTOVER RULE (sp020, non-negotiable): the four lines are DELETED from
config.common in the SAME commit that adds them to binds.py. Their i3 spelling
is added to config.d/zz-fallback-binds.conf so hotkeyd-panic.sh still gives
them back. $mod+Shift+s is base-not-overlay on purpose (dotfiles-13q: it was
stranded in native.conf once and WSL lost it) -- the fallback copy must keep
that property.

ACCEPTANCE
- hotkeyd/hotkeyd.sh check --ownership: no chord owned by both engines, under
  BOTH mod resolutions (test_no_chord_is_owned_by_both_i3_and_the_daemon
  already parametrizes this -- it should fail if a line is left behind)
- zero BadAccess on an :10-shaped display; grab count rises by 4
- i3 -C clean on the normal tree AND the panic-linked tree
- test-hotkeyd.sh, test-panic.sh, pytest all green

The i3 screenshot modes stayed with i3 as designed. Gates: pytest 344/0, test-hotkeyd 107/0, test-panic 54/0, test-nav-mode 40/0 both shapes, i3 -C clean on normal + panic-linked trees. title: sp020: system-mode cutover — $mod+0 becomes a ONE-SHOT hotkeyd layer (engine feature + bar)
notes:
SHIPPED as aef8d0e4, then applied to both live sessions.

SCOPE: $mod+0 plus the seven session actions behind it (lock, logout, switch_user, suspend, hibernate, reboot, shutdown). Unlike the three cutovers before it this is a MODE, not flat binds, so it needed an engine feature and a bar fix as well as a table edit.

ENGINE -- Layer.one_shot. i3 expressed one-shot by appending ', mode "default"' to every bind in the block. That is the LAYER being one-shot, not a per-bind choice; per bind it would be a per-bind opportunity to forget, on the one layer where forgetting leaves a bare 'r' on reboot. Implemented by APPENDING B.ExitLayer() to the matched action rather than assigning self._layer in _match_in_layer, so _run does both in order: the command still dispatches, and the single _publish afterwards sees the final state -- one published line for an event that both acts and leaves (hwds.2 contract). Only a bind that FIRES ends the layer; a key matching nothing is swallowed as in a persistent layer, so a typo does not silently drop you out.

BAR -- ModeBarTheme.resolve knew this surface ONLY by i3's long label string (indexOf('(l)ock')). The daemon publishes the layer name 'system', which fell through to the unknown-mode fallback: a strip with a pill and NO key hints, which looks fine at a glance. Both arms resolve now and both are load-bearing -- the short name is normal operation, the long one is what the bar sees while PANICKED, since the fallback hands the block back to i3 verbatim. Bar.qml needed no change: currentMode already prefers the daemon layer and inNavMode is false for 'system', so it passes straight through.

PRESERVED VERBATIM, named rather than fixed on a cutover: 'p' is shutdown while the mode's own label promises '(Shift+s)hutdown' and no Shift+s bind ever existed. That label is ALSO the string the bar matches on, so editing it silently blanks the hints during a panic. Filed as its own bug.

BLAST RADIUS, worse than any other layer's: entry needs a matched $mod+0, and dotfiles-ukyj is an OPEN, UNEXPLAINED report of the daemon entering nav on :10 from an event nothing physical produced. The same mechanism aimed here puts the next keystroke on a bare r/p. NOT NEW -- i3's mode had the identical shape and the identical bare keys -- but it moves with the binds, and ukyj should be read in that light.

MUTATION-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS: re-adding $mod+0 to config.common fails double-ownership under both resolutions; dropping it from the fallback fails fallback-parity under both; removing the one_shot arm from layers.py fails 4 of the 6 new engine tests; removing the 'system' arm from ModeBarTheme.resolve fails the new mode-bar assertion.

GATES: pytest 337/0, test-hotkeyd.sh 107/0, test-panic.sh 54/0, test-nav-mode.sh 40/0 both shapes, test-mode-bar.sh 106/0, hotkeyd.sh check OK (59 global binds, 2 layers, 31 layer binds, 106 chords).

LIVE APPLIED reload-before-restart on :0 and :10; both '59 chords grabbed ... via XI2', zero errors, $mod+0 among them.

LIVE VERIFICATION DELIBERATELY NOT DONE IN THE USER'S SESSION. Every bind here is destructive: if an injected $mod+0 entered the layer and the Escape failed, the user's next real keystroke would hit a bare r or p. Verified on a throwaway Xvfb :77 with its own daemon instead:
- entry/exit, SHIPPED table: super+0 -> {"layer":"system"}, Escape -> {"layer":"default"}.
- one-shot DISPATCH, scratch table (HOTKEYD_BINDS) with the same layer shape but 'echo >> file' payloads -- i3exit is machine-wide, not display-scoped, so even on :77 the real table would have locked or rebooted the actual session. super+0 -> layer=system; bare r -> the command RAN (file contains 'reboot') AND the layer returned to default in the same event.
:77 daemon stopped, Xvfb killed, log removed; :0 and :10 daemons confirmed still running afterwards (the hwds.23 scoping property).

title: sp020: directional-group cutover — $mod+hjkl/arrows focus and $mod+Shift+ move leave i3 for hotkeyd (the group T6 reverted)
notes:
SHIPPED as d46e598d, then applied to both live sessions.

SCOPE: 16 chords -- $mod+hjkl and $mod+arrows (focus), plus the $mod+Shift forms of both (move). THE GROUP T6 SHIPPED AND REVERTED (fd9e9f2).

WHY IT IS SAFE NOW AND WAS NOT THEN: T6's table hardcoded Mod4. On :10 $mod is Mod1, so the Mod4 forms were FREE -- the daemon grabbed and served them while i3 went on serving the Mod1 forms, a split invisible on :0 where the two agree. $mod resolves per display now (dotfiles-hwds.7), from the same i3wm.mod X resource i3 reads, so one table means Mod4 on :0 and Mod1 on :10 by construction.

THE OTHER OPEN RISK WAS MEASURED FIRST, NOT ARGUED: xrdp wraps every character in a synthetic Shift, which is why nav uses Ctrl as its move modifier -- so the 8 $mod+Shift+<letter> chords were gated on dotfiles-hwds.35, measured and closed before this cutover started. Six real RDP-client presses, six dispatches, tightest gap 1.88s. A passive grab matches (keycode, mask); it is not a modifier-STATE read, which is what nav's constraint was about.

Built from the same _DIRS / _ARROWS tables _nav_binds uses, so letters and arrows cannot drift apart, and neither can the global binds and the layer that does the same motions without a held modifier.

THE NAV LAYER STAYS. Not redundant: it moves focus with NO modifier held, and carries a resize sublayer with no global spelling.

CLOSURE, both resolutions: $mod+Ctrl+Left|Right was already the daemon's (workspace prev/next), nav's bare hjkl/arrows are layer-scoped not global, nothing else in the i3 tree binds these keysyms.

THE PARSER SENTINEL MOVED, SECOND TIME, SAME CAUSE. It was $mod+o until the nav cutover took it, then $mod+h under the reasoning that the directional group 'deliberately does NOT migrate' -- which this task did. A sentinel that is merely UNMIGRATED has an expiry date. Repointed at two chords i3 keeps by ARGUMENT: the panic chord (derived from B.PANIC_CHORD, and reserved in the validator, so a table binding it fails to load at all) and $mod+Shift+q (kill -- grabs die with the daemon, so the key for an already-misbehaving window stays where grabs cannot be lost).

MUTATION-VERIFIED THREE WAYS: re-adding $mod+Shift+k to config.common fails double-ownership under both resolutions; dropping it from the fallback fails fallback-parity under both; removing the kill sentinel fails the repointed parser test.

GATES: pytest 331/0, test-hotkeyd.sh 107/0, test-panic.sh 54/0, test-nav-mode.sh 40/0 both shapes, hotkeyd.sh check OK.

DAEMON 58 CHORDS, i3 23.

- focus: alt+l -> B, alt+h -> A, alt+Right -> B, alt+Left -> A.
- move:  alt+shift+l -> B|A*, alt+shift+h -> A*|B, alt+shift+Right -> B|A*, alt+shift+Left -> A*|B.

GATES: pytest 331/0, test-hotkeyd.sh 107/0, test-panic.sh 54/0, test-nav-mode.sh 40/0 on both $mod shapes, hotkeyd.sh check OK (30 global binds, 66 chords to grab).

LIVE APPLIED, reload-before-restart order (reversed, both engines own the group briefly and every workspace key double-fires with no BadAccess to warn): i3-msg reload on :0 and :10, then hotkeyd.sh restart on :0 and :10. Both logs report '30 chords grabbed ... via XI2', zero errors. The two BadAccess lines in hotkeyd-0.log are lines 1-4, pre-XI2-port history, not this restart.

LIVE VERIFIED on :10 (Mod1), each round-tripped back to the starting state:
- i3-command path: alt+ctrl+Right -> morning-challenge, alt+ctrl+Left -> dotfiles.

title: daemon survives its X server's death when idle — status lies and autostart cannot recover
design:
FOUND BY THE LIVE MATRIX (dotfiles-hwds.3) on the real machine, 2026-07-28.
This is the class of defect the matrix exists for: every suite is green.

OBSERVED CHAIN, all measured:
  :0 X server          GONE (xdpyinfo fails; that session ended)
  daemon pid 2199878   STILL RUNNING, 2h57m after its display died
  hotkeyd.sh status :0 reports "running on :0 (pid 2199878)", rc=0  <- a lie
  hotkeyd.sh start :0  refuses "already running on :0", rc=0        <- fatal
  lock                 /run/user/1000/hotkeyd-0.lock still held
  socket               accepts connections but NEVER REPLAYS state (2s+ timeout)

sp020 Task 4 success_criteria states the requirement plainly: "losing the X
connection exits the process (does not spin) so the launcher can restart it
([[adr0014]] fail-fast)". It did not exit.

WHY THIS IS USER-FACING AND NOT JUST A LEAK. i3's exec_always calls
`hotkeyd.sh start :0` on every session start and reload. The zombie holds the
flock, so start refuses, so the NEW :0 session gets NO daemon. Since the nav
cutover (71f6c4a8) i3 no longer owns mode "nav" -- so on the next physical
login at :0, nav is simply dead, silently, with the launcher reporting healthy.

The same shape hits :10 on an xrdp session restart.

WHY FAIL-FAST WORKS ELSEWHERE, WHICH IS THE CLUE. A daemon on a throwaway
display (:94) was observed exiting correctly within ~60s of its X server dying.
The difference is almost certainly ACTIVITY: the exiting daemon was pumping
events, so its next read hit the dead connection. An idle daemon blocked
waiting for an event it will never receive never learns the connection is gone.
So fail-fast is implemented on the event path only, and an idle daemon on a
dead display is invisible to it.

THREE THINGS TO FIX, and they are separable:

1. THE DAEMON must notice a dead X connection while idle. Options: a poll/select
   timeout on the X fd so the loop wakes periodically and can observe EOF; or
   watch the connection fd for HUP rather than only reading it on events. Note
   the daemon already sleeps -- dotfiles-hwds.27 added an idle reconcile branch
   -- so an idle wakeup path exists to hang this on.

2. `status` MUST NOT report healthy for a daemon whose display is gone. It
   currently reads only the process, never the display. A liveness check that
   cannot detect death is worse than none, because it is what an operator
   consults during an outage (the dotfiles-hwds.19/.21 lesson, again).

3. `start` MUST be able to recover. Refusing on a stale lock is right when the
   holder is alive and serving; it is wrong when the holder is a zombie on a
   dead display. Whatever the fix, it must not reintroduce the double-start
   hazard the flock exists to prevent -- see hwds.12 requirement 4 for the
   precedent that "stopped everywhere" beats "assume".

DO NOT paper over this by having the launcher pkill a stale daemon. That is the
unscoped-kill anti-pattern (dotfiles-8xt) sp020 bans, and dotfiles-hwds.23 has
just finished making the test suite stop doing exactly that.

REPRO: start a daemon on a throwaway display, kill the X server, leave the
daemon idle (inject nothing), and observe it still running minutes later while
status reports healthy and start refuses.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED: hypothesis 1 refuted and guarded; problems 2 and 3 fixed, one
commit each.

Branch: worktree-agent-a08817fe1d62af5ad
Worktree: /home/jan/.dotfiles/.claude/worktrees/agent-a08817fe1d62af5ad
Commits (oldest first):
  a92d1fa9  test(hotkeyd): pin the idle daemon's fail-fast on a dead X server
  0402fcf4  fix(hotkeyd): status must answer "serving", not "a process exists"
  a73120cc  fix(hotkeyd): start recovers a display whose daemon stopped serving

--- PROBLEM 1: REFUTED, then guarded (a92d1fa9) ---
No production change. Evidence in the DIAGNOSIS note above: five X-death modes,
idle daemon, exits in ~1 s every time. The idle branch has TWO independent
observers of the X connection and either suffices — d.pending_events()
(hotkeyd.py:1146) raises ConnectionClosedError at EOF, and d.fileno() in the
select() wait set re-raises the same stored error. Established by mutation:
swallowing pending_events alone STILL exits; only reducing the idle branch to a
bare sleep produces the reported symptom.
- test-launcher.sh: "an idle daemon exits when its X server dies (adr0014)".
  Honest labelling: this case PASSES on the unmutated tree. It is a guard, not
  a repro, and the commit message says so.

--- PROBLEM 2: status answers "serving", not "a process exists" (0402fcf4) ---
- hotkeyd.py SingleInstance: the lock file doubles as a HEARTBEAT. beat() from
  the top of run_daemon's loop, rate-limited to HEARTBEAT_PERIOD_S=1.0 so the
  key path pays nothing. flock answers "alive" (what pgrep already said); mtime
  answers "is the loop turning", which is the question an outage has.
- hotkeyd.py probe_display(): python-xlib only, shells out to NOTHING. Bounded
  by SIGALRM at PROBE_TIMEOUT_S=3.0. Measured: against a SIGSTOPped Xvfb,
  python-xlib blocks at protocol/display.py:561, which is select(timeout=None) —
  socket.setdefaulttimeout does NOT bound it (tried first, still hung 20 s).
- hotkeyd.py health() + `--health`, rc 0 / 6 / 7, runs BEFORE load_table.
  6 vs 7 is a safety boundary, not cosmetics: 6 is the daemon's own evidence
  about itself; 7 is only "the display did not answer US", which a caller with
  no XAUTHORITY produces against a healthy daemon.
- hotkeyd.sh status: exits 6 with the reason and the pid when not serving.
  Not 0 (the defect), not 1 (callers read 1 as "no daemon for this display").

--- PROBLEM 3: start recovers, precisely (a73120cc) ---
- hotkeyd.sh start: on finding a pid it asks health() and acts ONLY on rc 6,
  ending that ONE pid via reap_pid(). The pid comes from daemon_pid(), i.e. the
  daemon's own `--display` argv — the identification dotfiles-8xt's ban on
  unscoped kills explicitly permits. No pattern ever reaches kill. rc 7 refuses
  and touches nothing.
- reap_pid() shared with `stop` (which had the same escalation inline). SIGCONT
  first: a frozen daemon cannot act on SIGTERM until it runs again.
- Double-start hazard NOT reintroduced: the flock still decides who serves, and
  the suite asserts a SERVING daemon is still refused with no duplicate.

--- TEST NUMBERS ---
                       baseline (main)   after
  pytest                    310           322   (+12)
  test-launcher.sh          22/0          36/0  (+14)
  ./hotkeyd/test-hotkeyd.sh 107/0         107/0 (launcher is one stage there)

--- MUTATION EVIDENCE (each reverts ONE property) ---
M1 idle branch reduced to a bare sleep, both X observers removed
   -> "the idle daemon outlived its X server by >12s"          35/1
M2 status decides from daemon_pid() alone
   -> status cases red, incl. "status returns against a frozen X server rc=0"
                                                                34/2
M3 start refuses on rc 6 instead of reaping
   -> "start recovers a display ...", "the daemon ... was ended" red   33/3
M4 start reaps on rc 7 too (safety boundary removed)
   -> "the beating daemon was NOT reaped ...", "start refuses rather than
      replacing a beating daemon" red                           34/2
M5 SIGALRM disarmed in probe_display
   -> pytest test_the_display_probe_gives_up_instead_of_blocking FAILED,
      and "status hung on a frozen X server (20s, rc=124)"      33/3
M6 heartbeat removed from the run loop
   -> a SERVING daemon reads as wedged and start reaps it        34/2

A weaker first attempt at M1 (removing only the `except ConnectionClosedError`
clause) did NOT kill the guard — the daemon still exits, just with a traceback.
Recorded because it is the reason the guard's comment names both observers.

--- UNVERIFIED / CAVEATS ---
1. Nothing was verified on the live :0 or :10. The fix is exercised only under
   Xvfb. The `start` reap path in particular has never run against a real
   session.
2. HEARTBEAT_STALE_S=5.0 is a judgement, not a measurement. The worst
   legitimate stall on the loop is a blocking i3 command reply (I3Client
   _recv_reply has no timeout); if that ever exceeds 5 s, `start` would reap a
   daemon that was merely slow. Not observed, not bounded.
3. The frozen-daemon specimen is synthesised with SIGSTOP. It reproduces the
   OPERATOR-VISIBLE chain exactly (pid present, flock held, socket accepting,
   nothing served) but not any known way for a daemon to reach that state on
   its own — because, per the diagnosis, no such way was found.
4. `status` collapses health rc 7 into its own exit 6. Deliberate (status has
   one "not serving" verdict) but it does lose the 6/7 distinction for a caller
   reading status's code rather than its message.
5. LATENT, NOT FIXED, and worth its own issue: StatePublisher._current is None
   until the first layer change, so a healthy daemon that has not been used
   accepts a connection and replays NOTHING. That is what the report cited as
   "socket accepts connections but never replays state" and read as a zombie.
   A bar starting before the first nav sees a blank pill for the same reason.
   Fixing it means publishing the seeded starting state, which collides with
   test_a_freshly_started_daemon_replays_nothing_to_a_client (an intentional
   dotfiles-hwds.27 cause-2 guard), so it needs a decision, not a patch.

--- ENVIRONMENT NOTE ---
The specimen pid 2199878 no longer exists. Both live daemons were replaced at
11:15:44 and 11:15:45 (one second apart, the signature of a single i3
exec_always firing — one session's exec_always starts both). Panic is ruled out:
no /run/user/1000/hotkeyd-panic.displays and no fallback link in ~/.i3/config.d.
The session is healthy now — :0 pid 2444736, :10 pid 2444761, and hotkeyd-10.log
shows live nav transitions. All diagnosis evidence above was captured while the
original process was alive. The main checkout's hotkeyd/ is unmodified; every
change is confined to the worktree.
THIS TICKET WAS FILED ON A MISMEASUREMENT. I made the error; recording it in
full because the reasoning is more useful than the conclusion was.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE FALSE REPORT: xdpyinfo is NOT INSTALLED on this machine.
'DISPLAY=:0 xdpyinfo >/dev/null 2>&1' exits 127 (command not found). I read a
non-zero exit as 'X server GONE' and built the whole chain on it. Verified now:
xdpyinfo absent; Xorg :0 is pid 884, up 11 DAYS; a fresh Xlib Display(':0')
opens fine at 24-bit.

EVERY SYMPTOM IN THE ORIGINAL DESIGN WAS NORMAL BEHAVIOUR:
  'X server gone'                  -> alive the whole time
  'daemon running 2h57m on a dead
   display'                        -> just uptime; it started at 07:48
  'status lies, reports running'   -> it was TRUE
  'start refuses, cannot recover'  -> CORRECT: the holder was alive and serving
  'socket never replays'           -> normal before the first _publish; already
                                      pinned as intended by hwds.27's audit
  'resume manufactures a zombie'   -> it started a healthy daemon on a healthy
                                      display

The implementer refuted the diagnosis before writing a fix, which is exactly
what the brief asked for and what should happen more often. Its evidence:
pid 2199878 held an ESTABLISHED unix socket to /tmp/.X11-unix/X0 (fd 3) and to
:0's i3 (pid 1632, fd 7), and was LOOPING not blocked -- voluntary_ctxt_switches
+20 over 5s = 4/s, exactly the 0.25s idle select timeout.

THE STATED HYPOTHESIS IS ALSO FALSE. 'Fail-fast exists on the event path only,
an idle daemon never notices' -- tested directly across five death modes
(SIGTERM/SIGKILL, with and without real i3, immediately and after 15s idle),
daemon left idle: exits in ~1s EVERY time. The idle branch has two independent
observers of the X connection -- pending_events() raising at EOF, and the fd in
the select wait set where fileno() re-raises. Mutation confirmed: swallowing
one alone still exits; only reducing the idle branch to a bare sleep reproduces
the reported symptom.

The :94 observation that seeded the hypothesis (a daemon exiting when its X
server died) was therefore not a contrast with :0 -- it was the normal
behaviour, and :0 was normal too.

STATUS OF THIS TICKET: the defect as described does not exist. What the
implementer built is hardening against a state never observed in the wild --
see the next note for the merge decision, which is NOT automatic.
MERGE DECISION, taken by the user with the false premise on the table.

MERGED (cherry-picked to main as 1bb8de83 and its parent):
  a92d1fa9  test guard pinning the idle daemon's fail-fast. NO production
            change. Worth keeping precisely because the behaviour is now
            MEASURED (exits in ~1s across five death modes) rather than assumed.
  0402fcf4  lock-file heartbeat, probe_display(), --health, status rc 6/7.
            status can now distinguish 'a process exists' from 'it is serving'.

HELD BACK, deliberately not merged:
  a73120cc  start reaps a daemon whose heartbeat is stale.

WHY THE REAP WAS HELD. It auto-kills on a 5s heuristic that the implementer
itself flagged as a judgement rather than a measurement, on a path never run
against a real session, to defend against a state never observed in the wild --
because the state this ticket described does not exist.

THAT DECISION WAS VINDICATED WITHIN MINUTES. On merging the heartbeat, status
immediately reported BOTH of the user's healthy, serving daemons as NOT SERVING
-- they predated the heartbeat code, so they never wrote one. Had the reap
landed,  would have killed both working daemons on the user's live
session. Filed as dotfiles-hwds.29.

DO NOT MERGE a73120cc until hwds.29 is resolved AND HEARTBEAT_STALE_S has a
measured basis. Automatic recovery keyed off an unmeasured threshold, feeding
on a signal that is absent-by-default after any upgrade, is a worse failure
mode than the one it guards.

Live state after this work: daemons restarted onto the new build, :0 pid
2488501 and :10 pid 2487968, both reporting 'running' rc 0, nav verified
working on :10 via the state socket.
close_reason: Filed on my mismeasurement -- the defect does not exist. xdpyinfo is not installed here, so 'DISPLAY=:0 xdpyinfo' exits 127 and I read that as 'X server gone'. Xorg :0 is pid 884, up 11 days. The daemon was healthy and looping (4 ctx switches/sec = the 0.25s idle select), status was truthful, start was correct to refuse. The stated hypothesis was also refuted: idle fail-fast works, exiting in ~1s across five death modes. Two of three commits merged anyway on their own merit (1bb8de83): a test guard pinning the now-MEASURED idle fail-fast, and status distinguishing 'a process exists' from 'it is serving'. The third (a73120cc, start auto-reaps on a 5s heuristic) was deliberately NOT merged and must not land until dotfiles-hwds.29 is fixed -- on merge the heartbeat immediately reported both healthy live daemons as wedged, so the reap would have killed them.

title: test-panic.sh section 1b asserts a false premise — the panic suite is permanently RED at HEAD
description: Discovered during the audit of dotfiles-hwds.23 (parent for context; NOT caused by it).
design:
MEASURED at pristine main (4ff96794), exported to a temp dir and run with a
pgrep wrapper hiding only the live :0/:10 pids:

    panic: 41 passed, 1 failed
    FAIL expected the live daemon to keep the chord, got: i3

Identical failure on the dotfiles-hwds.23 branch (49 passed, 1 failed) and on
every mutant run. It is NOT a regression from .23 — it pre-exists and .23 does
not touch section 1b (test-panic.sh:265-283, unchanged in the diff).

WHY IT FAILS. 1b's premise is stated at test-panic.sh:267-271 and again in
section 3's header (:324-328): 'X refuses a second client the same chord'. That
is false, and dotfiles-f224 has the measurement: the X server keeps core and XI2
passive grabs in SEPARATE conflict domains (GrabMatchesSecond compares
grabtype), and the most recently added grab wins delivery. The daemon grabs via
XI2 (e149aa76), i3 grabs core on reload -- so the reload DOES take the chord and
the daemon does not keep it. The test asserts the opposite.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND f224. f224 tracks the grab-domain semantics and is
superseded in direction by dotfiles-hwds.25. Neither records the CONSEQUENCE:
test-panic.sh exits non-zero on a clean tree, so test-hotkeyd.sh stage 'panic'
is red at HEAD and its exit code carries no signal. A permanently red suite is
one nobody reads, and it means no post-merge gate can use it.

FIX -- REWRITE, DO NOT DELETE. 1b is the only case that makes 'no contested
window' a finding rather than a hope (the file header at :4-10 and section 3
both lean on it). Its INTENT still holds: panic's stop-before-reload ordering is
load-bearing. What changed is the observable. Under separate grab domains the
hazard is no longer 'i3 fails to get the chord' -- it is that BOTH clients hold
grabs and the winner flips to whoever grabbed last, which is exactly what f224
describes as the lost safety net. So 1b should assert the contested state
directly (daemon process still alive AND i3's loaded config carries the bind
after a reload-without-stop), not 'the daemon keeps the chord'.

Correct section 3's header comment in the same change -- it repeats the same
false premise.

Interim option if the rewrite waits on hwds.25: mark 1b an explicit known
failure so the suite's exit code becomes meaningful again. Do not simply delete
it.
notes:
DEVIATION (branch naming): dispatcher instructed one worktree for both dotfiles-1wti and dotfiles-8qju, one commit each. So this landed on worktree-agent-abd25eeaae3c26a88 rather than a bd-dotfiles-1wti.0 branch. Commit 63511179 is the whole of 1wti; nothing else is mixed into it.

DEVIATION (scope of what 1b can prove): the issue's design said 1b should assert 'daemon process still alive AND i3's loaded config carries the bind after a reload-without-stop'. Implemented that and went one step further -- a reload-without-stop leaving the bind loaded is not on its own proof that the DAEMON still holds a grab, only that i3 does. The unlink-and-hand-back step plus the pid-identity check is what closes that gap. Measured, not assumed: the daemon answers again with the same pid.

MEASURED, worth recording next to f224: inverting panic's stop/reload loops leaves an end state indistinguishable from the correct one -- 14 passed / 0 failed across sections 1-3 with the loops swapped, before this commit. The old 1b comment's claim that it guarded that ordering was never achievable post-hoc. Section 2's new line-order assertion is the replacement and does catch it (14/1).
close_reason:
AUDITED: APPROVED (independent re-measurement, reviewer agent)

CRITERIA VERIFIED
- 1b rewritten not deleted, and it does establish the contested state:
  hotkeyd/test-panic.sh:308-338. Step 1 (i3 takes the chord, daemon count 1),
  step 2 (unlink+reload hands it straight back), step 3 (pid identical).
  The single-ownership reasoning HOLDS: no re-grab path can fire between the
  two who_answers calls. hotkeyd.py:996 regrabs only on MappingNotify
  (and that is compare-then-regrab, hotkeyd.py:391-393 -- only a keycode that
  MOVED is re-registered), plus XI_HIERARCHY_CHANGED/XI_DEVICE_CHANGED
  (hotkeyd.py:1001-1003) and SIGHUP (hotkeyd.py:1076). An i3 reload triggers
  none of them; the i3 'mode' subscription (hotkeyd.py:944-968) feeds layer
  arbitration, not base grabs. So pid-identity + no-regrab-path together mean
  the daemon's XI2 grab was live THROUGHOUT step 1 -- two owners, reproduced.
- THE HEADLINE CLAIM, verified directly. Mutant 'panic stops nothing'
  (hotkeyd.sh stop reports success, kills nothing) -> 13 passed, 2 failed.
  The two failures are ONLY 'daemon survived panic on :81' and 'a daemon
  survived panic and contends with the fallback'. The assertion
  'I3 now answers Mod4+F10 -- ownership actually transferred' PASSED under
  that mutant. The old section-3 prose (:325-328 pre-commit) leaned on exactly
  that assertion to prove the daemon had let go; it cannot. The rewrite at
  :406-420 is justified.
- THE ORDERING FINDING, confirmed. Old suite (63511179^), sections 1-3:
  unswapped -> 10 passed / 1 failed; with panic's stop and reload loops SWAPPED
  -> 10 passed / 1 failed. IDENTICAL, same single failure ('expected the live
  daemon to keep the chord, got: i3'). The old 1b comment's claim to guard the
  ordering was vacuous, as stated. The new direct assertion at :358-369 DOES
  catch it: same mutant on the post-commit tree -> 14 passed / 1 failed, and
  that one failure is the ordering assertion alone.
- Mutant 'daemon restarted in the window' -> 14 passed / 1 failed, caught ONLY
  by the pid-identity check (:334-338). The pid check is not decorative.
- Baseline sections 1-3: 15 passed / 0 failed.

SUITE NUMBERS, all re-run by the reviewer
  hotkeyd/test-panic.sh    54 passed, 0 failed   (was 49/1 -- arithmetic checks:
                                                  50 assertions + 4 new = 54)
  hotkeyd/test-hotkeyd.sh  96 passed, 0 failed
  cd hotkeyd && pytest     282 passed
Live daemons 2199873 (:10) / 2199878 (:0) verified alive after every run.
All panic work ran under HOTKEYD_PGREP_SCOPE; sandbox copies only.

TAUTOLOGY SWEEP: none found. Each of the 4 new assertions has a mutant that

DEVIATIONS -- logged and acceptable
- branch naming: one worktree served both 1wti and 8qju per dispatcher

  not overlap in files.
- the section-2 ordering assertion reads panic's own trace rather than a WM

- dotfiles-v84s (stale fallback-is-empty comment at test-panic.sh:80-84) filed
  rather than fixed. Correct call: it justifies which fallback SOURCE the
  harness uses, touches no assertion, and the real fix reaches
  zz-fallback-binds.conf, outside the panic suite's file ownership.

title: i3/test-nav-mode.sh must be re-pointed at the daemon when mode "nav" leaves config.common
design:
i3/test-nav-mode.sh is entirely about i3's 'nav' MODE: it spawns a real i3 on config.common, presses super+o, and asserts focus/move/resize plus the 'nop nav-resize-on|off' marker binds reaching the bar's stream. Removing the mode "nav" block from i3/config.common (lines ~408-466 incl. the twelve 'nop nav-*' marker binds) invalidates the whole harness, not just a scenario — including its four PIXEL-level focus-ring assertions (import + histogram on 16A085 / CB4B16), which are the only end-to-end coverage of the red 'keys are captured' cue.

Those four scenarios also need a second change: dotfiles-hwds.2/.9 moved the ring off i3 mode events onto hotkeyd's layer socket, so 'nav' is no longer in qs-focus-border.py's COLOR_MODES ({'screenshot'} only). Driving them now requires a real hotkeyd daemon in the harness, publishing on $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hotkeyd-<display>.sock.

A working reference implementation of exactly that rewrite exists on the abandoned branch bd-dotfiles-hwds.2.0 (commit ebe19ae, i3/test-nav-mode.sh hunk): it sets XDG_RUNTIME_DIR to the harness TMP so the helper resolves the daemon's socket, and restores the four ring scenarios against it. It was dropped from bd-dotfiles-hwds.2.1 only because test-nav-mode.sh is owned by the i3-side cutover, not by the bar task, and main has since reverted the nav cutover underneath it.

Not urgent until config.common actually changes; urgent the moment it does.

title: daemon replayed layer=nav on a live session with nothing pressed and no modifier held
design:
Observed on the live xrdp :10 session immediately after the nav cutover
(dotfiles-hwds.16, commit 71f6c4a8) and the i3 restart that first started the
daemon there.

WHAT HAPPENED. ~30s after the daemon started, the first client to connect to
/run/user/1000/hotkeyd-10.sock was replayed:

    {"layer":"nav","mod":"resize"}

Nobody had pressed $mod+o. No modifier was physically held -- a root
query_pointer taken seconds later reported mask 0x0. A second connection made
immediately afterwards was replayed the correct state:

    {"layer":"default","mod":null}

and the daemon behaved correctly from then on (a subsequent injected
$mod+o / Escape produced a clean default -> nav -> default feed).

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC GLITCH. While the daemon believes it is in
a layer it GRABS THE LAYER'S BARE KEYS -- h, j, k, l, arrows, q, Escape,
Return. global_chords()'s docstring calls this out explicitly: grabbing those
permanently "would swallow those keys from every application for as long as the
daemon runs". A daemon that spontaneously believes it is in nav is a daemon
that eats hjkl from the user's editor and terminal. Self-correcting after ~30s
is luck, not a design property.

CANDIDATE CAUSES, none confirmed:
1. Spurious xrdp key delivery. dotfiles-hwds.24 measured that this session
   delivers every character as release-press-release, with a leading release
   that has no matching press. If such a burst can look like $mod+o, the daemon
   would enter nav without a real keypress. This is the strongest candidate and
   the two tickets should be read together.
2. Startup state. The daemon may publish or compute an initial layer/mod before
   it has read real modifier state, and the replay buffer then serves that.
3. An artifact of the i3 restart -- grabs are re-established while events may
   be in flight.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. The daemon logs nothing about layer transitions today.
Add a transition log (entered/left, with the triggering keycode, modifier mask
and source device id -- the XI2 port already resolves sourceid) and leave it
running on :10. If it recurs the log names the event that caused it; if the
trigger has no plausible physical origin, cause 1 is confirmed.

Do NOT close on "could not reproduce". It appeared once in the first minutes of
the first live run; the sample is one session.

RECOVERY IF IT RECURS, for whoever hits it: $mod+Shift+F12 (panic) hands the
keyboard back to i3 with the full nav block restored from
zz-fallback-binds.conf, then hotkeyd-panic.sh resume returns to the daemon.

Worktree: /home/jan/.dotfiles/.claude/worktrees/agent-ace2d931f4f780026

=== 1. DIAGNOSABILITY (the deliverable) ===

layers.py:format_transition() + LayerEngine._publish(ev, note). One line per
PUBLISHED state change -- not per assignment -- because what a bar was told is
the thing a recurrence has to be explained against, and a refused layer entry
(which publishes nothing) must not show up as a transition.

Real line off the live-X stage:

  hotkeyd: transition layer=default->nav mod=none->none trigger=press:o
    keycode=32 mask=0x0040 mods=Mod4 sourceid=5
    device='Virtual core XTEST keyboard' held=none i3_mode=default

  hotkeyd: transition layer=nav->nav mod=none->move trigger=press:Control_L
    keycode=37 mask=0x0000 mods=none sourceid=5
    device='Virtual core XTEST keyboard' held=Ctrl i3_mode=default

  hotkeyd: transition layer=nav->nav mod=move->none trigger=none held=none
    i3_mode=default note=reconcile:dropped=Ctrl

Fields and why each: keycode+mask are what X delivered BEFORE the keysym lookup
and BEFORE the lock-bit strip (the :10 keymap resets on every connect, so `key`
alone cannot identify the physical key, and a chord matched on a mask nobody
held is the cause-1 shape); sourceid+device are the only channel separating an
injected keystroke from a typed one; held+i3_mode are the two pieces of belief
that decide the sublayer and whether entry was allowed. Unresolvable fields
print `none` -- never a plausible stand-in, since cause 1 turns entirely on
provenance.

layers.Event gained keycode / raw_state (default None) purely to carry this.
No matching decision reads either. hotkeyd.to_event fills them; Daemon.pump
passes keycode=k.detail.

Always-on to stderr -> the launcher log. Volume is bounded: publish is
change-only, and in the default layer `mod` is structurally always None, so an
idle session logs nothing.

=== 2. THE THREE CANDIDATES ===

RULED OUT -- cause 2 (startup state served out of the replay buffer).
StatePublisher._current starts None and is set ONLY by LayerEngine._publish.
Nothing in Daemon.__init__, run_daemon, wire_i3_mode or sync_i3_mode publishes.
So a fresh daemon replays NOTHING to a connecting client, let alone a layer.
Pinned through the real StatePublisher on a real unix socket:
  test_daemon.py::test_a_freshly_started_daemon_replays_nothing_to_a_client
  test_daemon.py::test_constructing_the_daemon_publishes_nothing_at_all
  test_layers.py::test_a_fresh_engine_publishes_nothing_at_all_before_the_first_key

RULED OUT -- cause 3 (artifact of the i3 restart / grabs re-established).
pump_i3 is the entire surface an i3 restart touches. set_i3_mode can only ever
move the layer TO default; poll_events/sync_i3_mode never assign a layer at all.
Pinned with an i3 stub that reports a fresh connection on every poll and cycles
default/resize/default:
  test_daemon.py::test_no_i3_reconnect_or_mode_traffic_can_enter_a_layer
  test_layers.py::test_no_amount_of_i3_mode_traffic_can_enter_a_layer

The structural consequence: `self._layer = <non-default>` has exactly ONE
writer in the tree -- LayerEngine._run on a matched B.EnterLayer action. So the
daemon entered nav because it received and matched a Mod1+o PRESS. The question
is now exclusively "what produced that event", which is what the log answers.

NOT RULED OUT, NOT REPRODUCED -- cause 1 (spurious xrdp delivery, hwds.24).
I could not reproduce it. XTEST cannot reproduce xrdp's release-press-release
delivery (hwds.24 says so and it is right), and I will not invent a fix for an
unfalsified mechanism. What I can add to the ticket:

  (a) The observed state is COHERENT, not corrupt. On :10 $mod=Mod1 and nav's
      resize sublayer is Mod("Mod1") -- so {"layer":"nav","mod":"resize"} is
      exactly the state one press of Alt+o with Alt still down produces. It is
      not a garbled publish; it is what a real $mod+o looks like on :10.
  (b) binds.IGNORE_DEVICES ships EMPTY (deliberately -- see its comment). So an
      XTEST-injected $mod+o enters nav identically to a typed one. Any xdotool
      / harness / automation on :10 is a live producer of this exact state, and
      before this commit nothing recorded which it was. The ticket's own report
      notes an injected $mod+o was used minutes later on that same session.
      Pinned: test_daemon.py::test_an_injected_chord_is_logged_as_coming_from_
      the_xtest_device asserts the log names sourceid=5 / XTEST for such an
      event -- that is the discriminator a recurrence needs.
  (c) The "mask 0x0 seconds later" measurement is not evidence about the moment
      of entry: by then the daemon had already self-corrected.

=== 3. NO SPECULATIVE FIX ===
No change to the matching path, the grab path, or the coalescing question that
hwds.24 owns. Nothing claims to fix layer=nav.

=== 4. DEFENSIVE INVARIANT -- argued, and implemented in half ===

ARGUED FOR, held-modifier half. _expire_stale_holds runs only when an EVENT
arrives. That is right while keys flow and useless when they do not: an idle
daemon holding a phantom modifier keeps publishing -- and REPLAYING to every
late-connecting bar -- a sublayer nobody is in, with nothing scheduled that
would ever notice. That is precisely the shape of the observation (a state
served out of the replay buffer that corrected only once real events resumed).
The objection that X's mask is untrustworthy (layers.py's own docstring: the
mask ON an event is pre-event, a Ctrl release still carries the Ctrl bit) does
NOT apply to query_pointer: it is sampled outside any event, so there is no
event for it to be "pre". Cost: idle branch of the run loop only, never the key
path, at most ~4/s, and short-circuited to ZERO round-trips whenever the engine
believes nothing is held -- i.e. the whole session bar the seconds someone is
standing in a sublayer.

ARGUED AGAINST, layer half. X has no notion of `nav`, so there is nothing to
reconcile a layer against. A reconciler that dropped the layer on a modifier
mismatch would silently cancel a legitimate nav the user is standing in --
inventing the same class of state from the other direction. Not done, and
pinned as a negative: test_layers.py::test_reconcile_does_not_leave_a_layer,
test_daemon.py::test_the_reconcile_never_takes_the_layer_away.

RETRACT-ONLY, also argued. The server mask is ground truth about what is DOWN,
but _held is what this daemon has OBSERVED. Adding a hold it never saw pressed
would manufacture a sublayer out of a modifier belonging to some other client's
gesture. Pinned:
test_layers.py::test_reconcile_never_invents_a_hold_the_engine_never_observed.

Explicitly: this would NOT have prevented the observed layer=nav. It fixes the
`mod` half only.
