grep over all non-test hotkeyd/*.py returns 5 assignments: layers.py:182, 289,
420, 451 all assign DEFAULT_LAYER; layers.py:449 `self._layer = a.layer` is the
sole non-default writer, reachable only from _run() on an isinstance
B.EnterLayer action drawn from _match(). Checked the paths the brief named:
- SIGHUP (hotkeyd.py:1130-1144) constructs a BRAND-NEW LayerEngine -> default.
- --check (hotkeyd.py:1205-1206) returns before run_daemon; builds no engine.
- The new reconcile_holds does not touch _layer (pinned + mutation-tested).
Conclusion stands: the daemon entered nav because it matched a Mod1+o PRESS.

== 3. THE LOG IS DIAGNOSABLE IN PRACTICE -- VERIFIED ON A REAL SERVER

Fires on PUBLISHED changes only: the log call (layers.py:312) is inside
_publish AFTER the `if st == self._last_published: return` gate -- so not per
assignment, and a refused entry (_run continues without assigning, layers.py:
446-448 -> state unchanged) emits nothing.
Records all required fields. Captured live off Xvfb+i3 driving the REAL daemon:
  transition layer=default->nav mod=none->none trigger=press:o keycode=32
    mask=0x0040 mods=Mod4 sourceid=5 device='Virtual core XTEST keyboard'
    held=none i3_mode=default
keycode + raw mask (pre-keysym, pre-lock-strip) AND sourceid + device name are
all present and real. Unresolvable fields print literal `none` via _or_none
(layers.py:93) -- never a stand-in; I mutated `_or_none(ev.device_id)` to
`str(ev.device_id or 0)` and the suite caught it.

== 4. Event.keycode / raw_state ARE LOGGING-ONLY -- VERIFIED

grep for both across layers.py/hotkeyd.py/binds.py/live_check.py: the only
reads are layers.py:137-138 inside format_transition. _match, _match_in_layer,
_index and device_matches read key/mods/on_release/device only. No matching
decision reads either; logging did not change behaviour.

== 5. THE DEFENSIVE INVARIANT -- BOTH HALVES JUDGED SOUND

Zero round-trips when nothing is held: CONFIRMED. hotkeyd.py:1025 returns
before any X call. test_the_idle_reconcile_costs_no_x_round_trip_when_nothing
_is_held asserts pointer_queries == 0 after 10 calls; deleting the short
circuit fails a test (mutant run).
Retract-only cannot cancel a legitimate hold: CONFIRMED. `_held` can only ever
contain {Shift,Ctrl,Mod1,Mod4} (MOD_KEYSYMS, layers.py:35), and mods_from_mask
covers Shift/Ctrl/Mod1..Mod5, so every possible belief is representable in the
queried mask -- a genuinely-held modifier is corroborated, not dropped. Proven
live: with a real Ctrl down, "the server CONFIRMS it, so the reconcile retracts
nothing" PASSes. I also checked the guard-window interaction: reconcile
refreshes corroborated holds, but _expire_stale_holds already refreshed from
the same server state via `canon in ev.mods`, so this is a strict improvement,
not a weakening of the 120 ms guard.
The "would NOT have prevented the observed layer=nav" admission is CORRECT: the
reconciler provably cannot move the layer, so at best it would have turned the
bad replay into {"layer":"nav","mod":null} -- still a spontaneous nav grabbing
h/j/k/l. It is defence against the mod-half bug only, and the implementer
labelled it exactly that way rather than selling it as a fix. Arguing AGAINST
layer reconciliation is also right: X has no notion of `nav`, so a mismatch
reconciler would silently cancel a nav the user is standing in.

== 6. TESTS -- COUNTS AND MUTANTS INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED

pytest: 282 (main) -> 310. 28 added. VERIFIED by running both.
RED proof VERIFIED by replaying the new test files against the pre-fix tree:
24 failed / 286 passed, exactly as claimed (my run showed 32 failures; 8 were
artifacts of extracting only hotkeyd/, which makes test_binds.py's i3-config
assertions unresolvable -- 32-8 = 24).
The 4 green-pre-fix tests are, by name, exactly the cause-2/cause-3 rule-outs:
  test_a_freshly_started_daemon_replays_nothing_to_a_client
  test_constructing_the_daemon_publishes_nothing_at_all
  test_no_i3_reconnect_or_mode_traffic_can_enter_a_layer
  test_no_amount_of_i3_mode_traffic_can_enter_a_layer
They pin a ruling-out, not a fix, and are labelled as such. They do constrain:
the first drives a REAL StatePublisher over a REAL unix socket and asserts the
client recv TIMES OUT -- any startup publish would set _current and fail it.
MUTATION: I ran 6 of my own mutants, 6/6 caught, counts matching the claim
where the mutant was identical -- drop keycode from pump (2 tests), reconcile
also drops the layer (4), remove the idle short circuit (1), reconcile asserts
holds from the mask (1), fake the sourceid (caught), log even when unchanged
(caught, 14).
TAUTOLOGY SWEEP: read all 28. None tautological. They assert specific field
content and specific published state, and the engine fixture drives the REAL
shipped B.BINDS/B.LAYERS rather than a fabricated table. Weakest is
test_reconciling_holds_can_never_enter_a_layer (belt-and-braces negative in the
default layer) -- harmless, and the mutant it would miss is caught by
test_reconcile_never_invents_a_hold_the_engine_never_observed.
live: test-hotkeyd's live_check stage independently reproduced -- main 55 PASS
/ 0 FAIL, HEAD 66 PASS / 0 FAIL on isolated Xvfb+i3 displays. Delta = +11,
matching the claimed 95->106 (the 1 pre-existing failure is the
test-panic.sh one owned by dotfiles-1wti; that file was not touched).

== 7. dotfiles-l594 IS REAL, CORRECTLY SCOPED, RIGHTLY LEFT UNFIXED

Confirmed by reading hotkeyd.py:1135 -- SIGHUP replaces the engine but reuses
the same `pub`. The new engine seeds `_last_published = {"layer":"default"}`
so it will never publish `default` (not a change from its own seed), while
StatePublisher._current still holds the pre-reload layer and replays it to
every subsequent connect. Correctly scoped as NOT this bug's cause: I grepped
the repo and the ONLY SIGHUP senders are test-hotkeyd.sh:207/216 -- nothing in
hotkeyd.sh or the i3 config -- so that path never ran on :10. Leaving it
unfixed kept this diff auditable; that was the right call.

== HYGIENE ==
No TODO/FIXME/stub/skip/xfail/dead-code hits in the diff. The single broad
`except Exception` is the deliberate adr0014 swallow in reconcile_mods,
documented and pinned by test_a_failing_pointer_query_does_not_take_the_daemon
_down. Only the 5 permitted files touched; none of the sibling-reserved files
(test-panic.sh, test-hotkeyd.sh, test-launcher.sh, hotkeyd-panic.sh,
i3/test-nav-mode.sh) were modified. Live daemons 2199873 (:10) and 2199878
(:0) verified still running and untouched; all audit X servers were my own
throwaway displays.

DEVIATIONS: none. One logged scope note -- the log is per PUBLISHED state
change rather than per layer assignment. Accepted: it is a superset of
"entered/left" and additionally covers the `mod` half, which is what the
original observation ({"layer":"nav","mod":"resize"}) was actually about.

NOT A SPECULATIVE FIX: confirmed. No change to the matching path, the grab
path, or the coalescing question hwds.24 owns. Nothing claims to fix
layer=nav, and cause 1 is left explicitly open.

== WHY THIS CLOSES, GIVEN "Do NOT close on could-not-reproduce" ==
That instruction is honoured, not overridden. The mandated deliverable ("WHAT
WOULD SETTLE IT: add a transition log ... and leave it running on :10") is

standing watch -- leave the build running on :10, attribute a recurrence via
the transition line, do not close on could-not-reproduce -- has been moved
intact to dotfiles-ukyj (P1, open, discovered-from this ticket). If the user
would rather this ticket itself stay open, reopen it and close dotfiles-ukyj.

title: Single source of truth for global binds: declare owner in binds.py, generate i3's fragment
design:
User's design call (2026-07-28), rejecting the premise of dotfiles-f224.

f224 offered three ways to DETECT a chord owned by both i3 and the daemon
(runtime core-grab probe / static check --ownership / accept and document). The
user's response: "this should not happen at all." Detection accepts that the
state can exist; the requirement is that it structurally cannot.

WHY DETECTION IS NOT ENOUGH. Today binds.py and i3/config.common are two
hand-maintained lists of chords that can drift. Every mechanism proposed so far
-- BadAccess, check --ownership, the zz-fallback-binds.conf freshness test --
is a drift DETECTOR. The T6 revert was caused by exactly this drift, and it
passed every static check that existed at the time.

CONFIRMED, and it forces the shape of the fix: i3 4.25.1 has NO runtime unbind
and NO runtime bindsym. Verified empirically against a throwaway i3 -- the
command parser rejects both and dumps its full token list, which contains
neither. So a bind can only be removed from i3 by editing its CONFIG and
reloading. The config file is therefore the only lever, which means it must be
generated rather than hand-maintained if drift is to be impossible.

DESIGN. One chord, one declaration, one owner:

    Bind("$mod+h",       "focus left",        owner=I3)
    Bind("$mod+Shift+h", "move left",         owner=I3)
    Bind("$mod+o",       enter_layer("nav"),  owner=DAEMON)

- The daemon grabs ONLY owner=DAEMON entries.
- A generator emits the i3 fragment (i3/config.d/zz-generated-binds.conf) from
  owner=I3 entries; those lines leave config.common.
- A cutover becomes flipping one field and regenerating. A chord cannot appear
  in both lists because there is only one list.
- --check validates the declaration; the generated file is a build artifact,
  never hand-edited, and CI/pre-commit asserts it matches its source.

SCOPE -- the GLOBAL table, measured:
  142 bind lines in config.common
   -67 inside mode {} blocks  -> NOT global binds; these are what daemon LAYERS
                                 replace as groups migrate. Out of scope here.
  = 75 top-level bindsym      -> this task
   (11 use --release, already expressible as on_release=True)
   (12 bindcode are nav's nop markers, deleted by .16 regardless)

Bind()'s existing surface covers all 75 plus the new owner field. No new action
kinds are needed.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THE PLAN.
- Makes .16 structurally safe: instead of a two-file edit across ~18 chords
  where forgetting one is the T6 failure, it is a field flip that --check
  validates.
- Largely retires dotfiles-hwds.15 (check --ownership) as a DRIFT detector --
  double ownership becomes unrepresentable. .15 may survive in reduced form as
  a validator that the generated file matches its source, which is a much
  smaller thing.
- Retires f224: with one source there is nothing for a runtime probe to detect.
  Do not close f224 until this lands; it records the measurement that motivated
  this.
- ft003 owns i3 config layering and must be updated: config.d/ gains a
  GENERATED file, which is new for that feature.

RISKS.
- config.common is heavily commented, and those comments carry real design
  history (the xrdp Mod1 notes, the nop marker rationale). Generation must not
  discard them -- either carry comments through the declaration or leave the
  commentary in config.common around the generated include.
- A generated file in config.d/ interacts with zz-fallback-binds.conf's zz-
  ordering and with the panic path. Check both.
- 75 chords is a large mechanical change; it wants its own verification that
  the generated output is byte-equivalent in EFFECT to what it replaces
  (i3 -C plus a bind-by-bind diff of what i3 actually loaded, via GET_CONFIG
  including included_configs -- see hwds.12's technique).
notes:
STOP — LIKELY OBSOLETE (2026-07-28), measured.

This task existed to make double ownership structurally impossible, because
under CORE grabs a chord in both i3 and binds.py meant BadAccess and the T6
failure. Measured on a rebuilt T6 geometry (Xvfb, $mod=Mod1 as on :10, i3
owning $mod+h focus, $mod+o contested, the REAL shipped daemon and table):

    before: focused width 512
    after : focused width 461   <- Mod1+h inside nav RESIZED

The daemon WON. Under core grabs this was BadAccess and Alt+h fell through to
i3's focus, which is what reverted T6 (fd9e9f2).

WHY: layer chords are grabbed only while the layer is ACTIVE (chords_for /
global_chords) and re-synced on every transition. So the daemon grabs Mod1+h at
layer ENTRY -- after i3 grabbed at config load -- and XI2 vs core do not
conflict, later grabber wins. On layer exit the daemon ungrabs and i3's core
grab is still there, so focus works again.

That is exactly the i3-binding-mode semantics the whole migration was trying to
reproduce, and it now falls out of the mechanism for free. Double ownership of a
LAYER chord is no longer a defect; it is the design.

DO NOT RESUME without re-justifying. The remaining argument for a single source
is hygiene (drift between two hand-maintained lists), not correctness. That is a
much weaker case and does not warrant a 75-chord refactor.
close_reason: Obsolete, measured. Existed to make double ownership structurally impossible because under CORE grabs a chord in both i3 and binds.py meant BadAccess and the T6 failure. The XI2 port changed the mechanism: layer chords are grabbed only while the layer is active, the daemon grabs at layer entry (after i3), XI2 and core do not collide, later grabber wins. Verified on a rebuilt :10 geometry -- Alt+h inside nav resizes (512 -> 461). Double ownership of a layer chord is now the design, not a defect. The nav cutover shipped WITHOUT this 75-chord refactor. Remaining argument is hygiene, not correctness; re-file on its own merits if wanted.

title: xrdp delivers each character as release-press-release on :10 — may double-fire on_release binds
design:
Observed during the live sourceid measurement on :10 (2026-07-28). NOT yet
confirmed as a defect -- it is an observation on the RAW event stream that needs
re-checking through the GRAB path before anyone acts on it.

WHAT WAS SEEN. A passive XI2 raw-event probe, human typing at a real RDP client,
showed every character arriving as a THREE-event burst with a spurious LEADING
release:

    1798.1  release  a      <- release with no preceding press
    1798.2  press    a
    1798.3  release  a

and again mid-Shift-hold:

    5012.4  release  a
    5012.5  press    a
    5012.5  release  a

All three land within 0.2 ms, i.e. almost certainly the same X timestamp (X time
has 1 ms resolution).

WHY IT MIGHT MATTER.

1. on_release binds. ft011 publishes Bind(chord, action, on_release=True), and
   i3 currently has two live --release binds ($mod+Print, $mod+Shift+d). If the
   daemon sees release-press-release for one keypress, an on_release bind could
   fire TWICE per press on :10. us019 AC2 is specifically about
   release-triggered binds working, so this is on the acceptance path.

2. It interacts with the coalescer that dotfiles-hwds.13 REMOVED. The old
   Daemon.pump coalesced a same-timestamp, same-keycode release+press pair --
   which is exactly the shape of events 1798.1/1798.2. The XI2 port removed that
   machinery on the (correct, for auto-repeat) grounds that XI2 signals repeat
   via XIKeyRepeat and sends no synthetic release. But xrdp's pattern is not
   auto-repeat; it is delivery. So the port may have removed the thing that was
   incidentally absorbing it.

WHY IT IS NOT YET A DEFECT.

The probe monitors RAW events (XIRawKeyPress/Release on the root), which report
what the server received. A GRABBED key is delivered as XIDeviceEvent through
the grab, and the two paths need not carry the same event sequence. Nothing here
was measured through a grab. Also, no daemon was running on :10 during the
probe, so nothing was grabbed at all.

Reading the raw stream as if it were the grab stream is exactly the class of
inference that produced the wrong migration order in T6. Do not skip the check.

HOW TO SETTLE IT.

1. On :10, grab one throwaway chord with a press-triggered bind and one with
   on_release=True. Have a human type the chord. Count dispatches.
   Expect 1 each; more than 1 on the release bind confirms it.
2. If confirmed, decide where it belongs: re-introducing same-timestamp
   coalescing for the release path only, or a debounce in the engine. Note that
   dotfiles-hwds.4's fairness tests exist precisely to stop coalescing from
   eating GENUINE fast double-taps -- any fix must keep those green.
3. Cannot be settled by injection. XTEST does not reproduce xrdp's delivery
   pattern; that is the whole reason this was found by a human typing.

RELATED: dotfiles-hwds.3 (live matrix, owns :10 verification), hwds.4
(coalescer fairness), hwds.13 (removed the coalescer).
notes:
PROMOTED P2 -> P1 by dotfiles-hwds.33. This stopped being a speculative observation: the entry-point cutover moved $mod+Shift+d (bar restart) OUT of i3 and INTO hotkeyd/binds.py as an on_release bind, so the daemon now owns one of the two live --release binds this issue names, on :10.

TRACED THROUGH THE ENGINE, not inferred. Feeding the observed burst to LayerEngine.handle():
  release d -> _down.pop (absent) -> _match(on_release=True) -> FIRES
  press d   -> _is_repeat False (just popped) -> records _down -> no press bind -> nothing
  release d -> _match(on_release=True) -> FIRES AGAIN
Demonstrated, not argued: dispatched ['nop restart-bar', 'nop restart-bar'].
_is_repeat guards the PRESS path only; nothing dedups releases at all.

STILL UNCONFIRMED THROUGH THE GRAB PATH, so no guard was written. The original observation is off the RAW event stream, and it cannot be settled by injection because XTEST is what every harness here injects with while the question is about xrdp's own delivery. Needs a human at a real RDP client (dotfiles-hwds.3 / sp020 T15): press $mod+Shift+d ONCE on :10 and count quickshell restarts.

PINNED: hotkeyd/test_layers.py::test_an_xrdp_release_press_release_burst_fires_an_on_release_bind_once, xfail(strict=True). Suite stays green while the bug stands, and flips to a hard failure the moment a guard lands so the marker cannot outlive the fix.

WHERE A FIX BELONGS: Daemon.pump, not the engine. Event is X-agnostic and carries no timestamp; KeyEvent.time still exists at that layer. That is the same-timestamp coalescer dotfiles-hwds.13 removed -- correctly for auto-repeat (XI2 signals repeat via XIKeyRepeat and sends no synthetic release), incidentally for this. Note a genuine same-keycode release cannot repeat within one X millisecond without an intervening press, so same-(keycode,time) release dedup has no legitimate victim.

INTERIM: harmless if it does reproduce -- a doubled qs-start.sh is a redundant bar restart, not corruption, and qs-start.sh is flock/pkill-guarded. $mod+Print (region screenshot) is the other --release bind and is STILL i3-owned, so it is unaffected by the cutover.
close_reason: CONFIRMED as a real double-fire, then fixed in cd241427. The filing said 'may double-fire, needs re-checking through the grab path'; the unit test added with the fix shows the doubled dispatch directly (['nop shot','nop shot'] for one keypress). Fixed by requiring that the engine saw the key go down before an on_release bind matches, rather than by a time window — the burst shares one X timestamp so a coalescer would have to guess a threshold. Also covers a daemon starting or reloading while a key is held. Press binds and exit_keys untouched (both match on the press path). Verified live on :10 afterwards: $mod+Print fires exactly once.

title: XI2 grabs do not contend with i3's core grabs — ownership overlap is now silent
design:
MEASURED during dotfiles-hwds.13 (XI2 port), Xvfb + X.Org, python-xlib 0.33:

  client A core-XGrabKey Mod4+F11, then client B XIGrabKeycode the same chord
    -> B's reply reports ZERO failed modifiers (no BadAccess)
    -> injected Mod4+F11: A got 0 events, B got 3
  reverse order (XI2 first, core second) -> the CORE grabber wins, XI2 gets 0
  XI2-vs-XI2 across two clients DOES conflict -> reply.modifiers non-empty

The X server keeps core and XI2 passive grabs in separate conflict domains
(GrabMatchesSecond compares grabtype) and the most recently added grab wins
delivery (AddPassiveGrabToList prepends; CheckPassiveGrabsOnWindow walks from
the head).

sp020's mechanism amendment and dotfiles-hwds.13's pre-dispatch correction #4
both assert the opposite ('an XI2 passive grab contends with i3's core passive
grab identically'). Both are wrong and ft011 + i3/config.d/{native,wsl}.conf
were corrected in .13.

WHAT THIS COSTS: the BadAccess signal was the mid-cutover safety net — a chord
owned by both i3 and binds.py used to no-op on the daemon side and stay with
i3. It now silently transfers to whichever client grabbed last, which in
practice is the daemon (i3 grabs at config load, the daemon starts after). The
one chord in that state today is $mod+o (binds.py + i3/config.common:408).

WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT — pick one, do not do nothing:
1. Lean entirely on sp020 Task 13 / dotfiles-hwds.15 (`check --ownership`), the
   machine-generated ownership map. It never depended on BadAccess and is
   already the declared gate on every cutover commit. Cheapest, and probably
   right — but it is a STATIC check, so it cannot see an i3 reload at runtime.
2. Add a runtime core-grab PROBE to XAdapter.grab_key: attempt a core XGrabKey
   on the chord first, treat BadAccess as 'another client owns this', ungrab
   and then take the XI2 grab. Restores the runtime diagnostic exactly. Costs a
   round trip per chord per sync and a brief window holding a core grab.
3. Accept it explicitly and document that panic ($mod+Shift+F12) is the only
   runtime recovery, which is already true.

Blocked on nothing. Should be decided BEFORE the directional-group cutover
(dotfiles-hwds.16), because that is the commit where an unnoticed double-owned
chord does the most damage.
notes:
SUPERSEDED IN DIRECTION by dotfiles-hwds.25. The user rejected all three options
here on the grounds that double ownership 'should not happen at all' --
detection accepts the state can exist, and the requirement is that it cannot.

Additional measurement taken while deciding: i3 4.25.1 has NO runtime unbind and
NO runtime bindsym. Verified against a throwaway i3; the command parser rejects
both and dumps a full token list containing neither. This forces the shape of
.25: a bind can only leave i3 via its CONFIG plus a reload, so the config must
be generated rather than hand-maintained.

Keep this issue open until .25 lands -- it holds the grab-domain measurement
(core and XI2 passive grabs are in separate conflict domains, later grabber
wins, symmetric) that everything downstream depends on. Close it when single
ownership is structural.
close_reason: Superseded: there is nothing left to detect. This recorded that core and XI2 passive grabs occupy separate conflict domains (later grabber wins, symmetric) and asked how to detect a chord owned by both i3 and the daemon. After the nav cutover they share no chord, and the same measurement showed a shared LAYER chord is harmless by design -- the daemon shadows i3 while the layer is active and i3 regains it on exit, which is the i3-binding-mode semantics the migration was reproducing. The measurement itself is preserved in sp020 ## solution and ft011. Re-open only if a future migration reintroduces a genuinely contested chord.

title: test suite's panic sections stop the user's live :0/:10 daemons — process half is not sandboxed
design:
Production-facing sibling of dotfiles-f2be. That one is about sibling AGENT
worktrees contaminating each other's state file; this is about the test suite
reaching the USER'S LIVE SESSION, and it got sharper the moment autostart was
armed (a76e9a9).

MECHANISM
test-panic.sh sandboxes the FILE half correctly: HOME is overridden to $T/home
(test-panic.sh:76) before HOTKEYD_I3_CONFIG_D is derived from it (:78), and
HOTKEYD_FALLBACK_SRC points at a test table, so the fallback link lands in a
temp dir and never touches ~/.i3/config.d.

The PROCESS half has no equivalent override. hotkeyd-panic.sh target_displays()
(:83-89) is machine-wide by design -- it pgreps every 'hotkeyd.py .*--display'
on the box, which is correct for real recovery (the .12 requirement-4 decision:
panic must stop every display or another display can reload into the fallback
while its daemon still holds grabs). panic then runs '$LAUNCHER stop $d' for
each target (:116-118).

CONSEQUENCE
Running ./hotkeyd/test-hotkeyd.sh on the desktop, where autostart now keeps
daemons on :0 and :10, stops those real daemons. The suite's own panic sections
reach them. i3's exec_always brings them back only on the next reload, so the
live session silently loses hotkeyd for the rest of the session.

IMPACT TODAY: near zero. The daemon owns nothing -- $mod+o is contested and i3
wins it at config load, so a stopped daemon changes no behaviour.

IMPACT AFTER dotfiles-hwds.16: running the test suite kills the directional
group's bindings mid-session. That is the point where this becomes a real
footgun rather than a curiosity.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY 'SCOPE target_displays'
Narrowing it in production would break the machine-wide guarantee panic exists
to provide, and dotfiles-f2be already rules that out as a fix direction. The fix
belongs on the test side or in an explicitly test-only scoping hook.

OPTIONS (not decided here)
1. A HOTKEYD_PGREP_SCOPE / HOTKEYD_TARGET_DISPLAYS override that the suite sets
   and production never does -- explicit, greppable, and the same shape as the
   three overrides the scripts already carry.
2. Run the panic sections inside a PID or mount namespace so pgrep genuinely
   cannot see the host's daemons.
3. Guard: refuse to run the panic suite when a daemon is live on :0 or :10, with
   a message saying so. Cheapest, and it fails safe rather than silently.

RELATED: dotfiles-f2be (same root, agent-vs-agent), dotfiles-hwds.20 (which
widened resume's reload set for the mirror-image reason).
notes:
IMPLEMENTED: option 1 — HOTKEYD_PGREP_SCOPE, a test-only allow-list that FILTERS
the machine-wide pgrep enumeration in hotkeyd-panic.sh. Production never sets it
and target_displays() is not narrowed.

Branch bd-dotfiles-hwds.23.0, commit 056810fc.
Files: hotkeyd/hotkeyd-panic.sh (+44), hotkeyd/test-panic.sh (+189/-12).

WHY THIS OPTION
- Same shape as the three overrides the scripts already carry (HOTKEYD_FALLBACK_SRC,
  HOTKEYD_I3_CONFIG_D, HOTKEYD_X11_UNIX) — one more fence on the same wall,
  greppable, and the unset path is `cat`.
- A FILTER, not a replacement: the enumeration still runs in full and still has to
  DISCOVER each daemon by pgrep. A HOTKEYD_TARGET_DISPLAYS that replaced the
  enumeration would make section 8 ("panic stopped the daemon on the display it was
  not called with") a restatement of a list the test handed in.
- Applied at three points: target_displays(), all_displays(), and resume's target
  derivation (a stale state file must not walk past the fence into hotkeyd.sh start).

REJECTED
- PID/mount namespace: needs unshare/root-ish setup on every box the suite runs on
  (adr0002 condition 1 — this must run on a fresh box), and it would hide the very
  enumeration under test rather than scope it. It also fixes nothing for a human
  running the suite outside the namespace.
- Refuse-to-run guard when :0/:10 has a daemon: fails safe but makes the panic suite
  UNRUNNABLE on the one machine it matters on — autostart keeps :0/:10 armed, so the
  guard would skip the suite permanently and the coverage would rot unnoticed. It
  also does nothing for dotfiles-f2be, where the foreign daemon is on :8x.
- Narrowing target_displays() in production: explicitly ruled out by .12 and f2be.

ACCEPTANCE PROOF (the criterion: full ./hotkeyd/test-hotkeyd.sh must leave live
:0/:10 daemons running)

title: Directional-group cutover (supersedes the reverted T6)
design:
### Task 14: Directional-group cutover (supersedes Task 6)

#### bd
(none yet — `dotfiles-zgs4` is closed and its merge reverted; mint a fresh id)

#### type
refactor

#### effort
6h

#### depends
Task 13

#### files_touched
- `hotkeyd/binds.py` (directional group + nav layer active)
- `i3/config.common` (directional globals, `mode "nav"` block, and all twelve
  `nop` marker binds removed)
- `i3/test-nav-mode.sh` (re-pointed at the daemon)
- `docs/notes/im009.md` (approach/api_surface follow reality)

#### success_criteria
- one commit moves the whole grab-ownership closure — `$mod+{h,j,k,l}`,
  `$mod+{Left,Down,Up,Right}`, `$mod+Shift+*` moves, `$mod+q`, `$mod+o`, and
  the entire `mode "nav"` block — out of i3 and into `binds.py`; no chord
  exists in both at that commit (AC6)
- `hotkeyd.sh check --ownership` exits zero for **both** display shapes on the
  post-cutover tree, and the commit is rejected otherwise
- the daemon obtains every grab it requests on an `:10`-shaped display: zero
  `BadAccess`, asserted, not logged. This is the assertion whose absence let
  the reverted cutover merge green
- `$mod+h` resolves by state on both shapes: `focus left` in the default layer,
  `resize shrink width 5 px or 5 ppt` in nav's resize sublayer — the two
  meanings one grabber gives one chord
- `i3/test-nav-mode.sh` passes against the daemon while still asserting real
  effects: focus moves, window moves, resize deltas read from
  `i3-msg -t get_tree` geometry
- all three layers behave as before: bare `hjkl`/arrows focus, Ctrl moves, Alt
  resizes at 5px/5ppt, `q`/`Escape`/`Return` leave the layer with or without a
  modifier held
- resize is reachable on `:10` **without** Super — the `$altmod` workaround
  (`46e26e9`) is not reintroduced, since the RDP client captures that key
- `i3 -C` passes and no `nop nav-` string remains anywhere in `i3/` or
  `quickshell/`

#### edge_cases
- entering nav while Ctrl is already held
- Alt+`hjkl` at a container edge (no-op resize must not exit the layer)
- rapid layer enter/exit
- xrdp's per-character Shift synthesis during a nav session
- `$mod` = `Mod1` on `:10` with Alt as the resize modifier — the exact
  collision that reverted T6; must now be one grabber, two meanings
- i3 reload mid-layer
- a fresh clone where `zz-fallback-binds.conf` must still name the *pre-cutover*
  set (Task 10's freshness test has to be updated in this commit, not after)

#### test_plan
Two oracles, because the reverted attempt had only one. **Behaviour:**
`i3/test-nav-mode.sh` re-pointed, still asserting geometry and focus, plus a
per-layer leak case (bare `h` after releasing Ctrl must focus, not move) and
`q`-exits-while-Ctrl-held. **Ownership:** every behaviour case runs on an
`:10`-shaped display with `$mod` = `Mod1`, and the suite asserts zero
`BadAccess` plus a clean `check --ownership` before any behaviour assertion is
believed. A green behaviour run on a display where the daemon holds no grabs is
the exact false pass being designed out. Panic is exercised post-cutover: panic,
assert i3 serves the directional chords again, resume, assert the daemon does.
notes:
OPEN QUESTION for this task's verification, raised 2026-07-28, deliberately NOT
measured (user parked further probing to get back to the chain).

This task migrates $mod+Shift+{h,j,k,l} (the move binds) as part of the
directional group. A live XI2 probe on :10 showed xrdp DROPPING Shift mid-burst
to deliver a character:

    5012.5  press    a
    5012.6  release  Shift_L    <- dropped to deliver the character
    5910.4  release  Shift_L    <- physical release ~900 ms later

If the same drop can land around a chord press, $mod+Shift+h may arrive at the
grab with no ShiftMask -- matching the FOCUS bind instead of MOVE, since on :10
$mod is Mod1 and both are in this group. That would make the move half of the
directional group unreachable on the display in daily use.

This is a grab-mask question, NOT the held-modifier guard question (which is
settled: see hwds.3, the ~120 ms guard is permanent). It is unmeasured.

CHEAP TO SETTLE, and it should be settled BEFORE the cutover commit rather than
during it: passive probe on :10, human presses Alt+Shift+h a few times and Alt+h
as a control, read whether ShiftMask is present on the h press. 30 seconds of
typing. Finding this during .16 instead of before it is the T6 pattern -- a :10
problem discovered after the commit landed.

Probe already written and validated: scratchpad srcprobe.py (passive XI2 raw
monitoring, takes no grabs); it would need extending to report the modifier
state alongside sourceid.
SHIPPED AND VERIFIED LIVE (2026-07-28), commit 71f6c4a8.

SCOPE THAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED — smaller than this task was re-scoped to. The
directional group (i3's global $mod+hjkl focus/move) was NOT migrated and does
not need to be. Only the original T6 scope shipped: $mod+o and the mode "nav"
block, including the twelve nop nav-* markers, removed from config.common;
binds.py LAYERS["nav"] is now sole owner.

WHY THE GROUP WAS UNNECESSARY. The XI2 port (hwds.13) changed the mechanism.
Core and XI2 passive grabs sit in separate conflict domains and the later
grabber wins; layer chords are grabbed only while the layer is ACTIVE, so the
daemon grabs at layer entry -- after i3 grabbed at config load -- and wins. On
exit it ungrabs and i3's globals work again. That reproduces i3-binding-mode
semantics without moving i3's binds at all.

EVIDENCE, in order of strength:
1. LIVE on the user's real xrdp :10 session after an i3 restart. i3's
   get_binding_modes no longer lists nav. Daemon running (pid 2199873, socket
   /run/user/1000/hotkeyd-10.sock). Driving $mod+o then Escape produced the
   full state feed:
       {"layer":"default","mod":null}   <- replay on connect
       {"layer":"nav","mod":null}       <- entered
       {"layer":"default","mod":null}   <- exited
   User confirmed nav works by hand.
2. Rebuilt :10 geometry (Xvfb, i3wm.mod: Mod1, real daemon and table), both
   with i3 contesting $mod+o and after removal: Alt+h inside nav RESIZES the
   focused window (width 512 -> 461) rather than moving focus. That is the
   exact gesture whose failure reverted T6.
3. pytest 281 -> 282; i3 -C clean on the base tree and on the composed tree
   with the panic fallback linked.

FALLBACK UPDATED, and the freshness test forced it rather than discipline:
zz-fallback-binds.conf now carries the removed nav block verbatim. Grabs die
with the daemon, so with i3 no longer owning nav a dead daemon means NO nav
until something restores it. test_binds.py failed until this was added.

NOT AUDITED INDEPENDENTLY. This was implemented inline rather than through the
implementer/reviewer pipeline. The live verification is strong evidence but it
is not an audit -- an independent pass should still check the removed block
against binds.py bind-for-bind, and confirm the panic path restores nav.

OPEN REGRESSION until dotfiles-hwds.2: the bar's nav pill and qs-focus-border's
red ring read i3 mode events and now show nothing. Task in flight.
close_reason: Shipped and verified live (71f6c4a8). nav left i3/config.common and hotkeyd owns it; confirmed on the user's real :10 session (i3 get_binding_modes no longer lists nav; $mod+o drives the daemon's layer; state feed default->nav->default) and on a rebuilt :10 geometry where Alt+h inside nav resizes rather than moving focus -- the exact gesture that reverted T6. The directional group was NOT migrated and does not need to be: XI2 layer chords shadow i3's globals only while a layer is active. Smaller scope than this task was re-scoped to, deliberately.

title: check --ownership: machine-generated chord ownership map
design:
### Task 13: `check --ownership` — the machine-generated chord ownership map

#### bd
(none yet — mint at re-ready)

#### type
feature

#### effort
4h

#### depends
Task 12

#### files_touched
- `hotkeyd/hotkeyd.sh` (`check --ownership` verb)
- `hotkeyd/hotkeyd.py` (map generation)
- `hotkeyd/test-hotkeyd.sh` (extend)

#### success_criteria
- emits, per display, one row per chord: chord → resolved modifier → owner in
  `{i3, daemon, neither, BOTH}`, generated by parsing i3's live bind table and
  `binds.py` — never hand-maintained (AC4)
- exits non-zero on any `BOTH` row, naming every offending chord
- run against the pre-T6 tree it reproduces the historical collision: the eight
  `Mod1+{h,j,k,l,Left,Down,Up,Right}` chords report `BOTH` on the `:10` shape
  and `neither`/`daemon` on the `:0` shape. This is the regression fixture — it
  is what proves the tool would have blocked T6
- resolves both display shapes in one invocation, so a `:0`-only run cannot
  report clean while `:10` collides
- a chord i3 owns via an overlay (`config.d/*.conf`, `config-xrdp`) is
  attributed to i3, not missed because only `config.common` was parsed

#### edge_cases
- i3 not running (must parse the config tree statically and say so)
- a chord i3 binds inside a `mode` block (owned only while that mode is active —
  reported distinctly, since it is the Task 9 arbitration case, not a collision)
- commented-out binds in the i3 tree (must not count as owned)
- `bindcode` entries alongside `bindsym` (keycode vs keysym normalisation)
- a chord in neither table (reported `neither`, not omitted)

#### test_plan
The historical fixture is the centrepiece: check out the pre-T6 `binds.py` and
`config.common` into a fixture dir and assert the tool exits non-zero naming the
eight chords. A tool that merely exits non-zero on *something* would pass a
weaker test, so the assertion names the exact chord set and the display it
collides on. Negative fixture: the current tree must exit zero, so the tool
cannot be satisfied by always failing. Mode-block chords asserted as their own
category rather than folded into `BOTH`.
notes:
SCOPE LIKELY REDUCED by dotfiles-hwds.25 (single source of truth). If binds.py
becomes the sole declaration and i3's fragment is generated from it, double
ownership is unrepresentable and this task's core purpose -- detecting a chord
in BOTH tables -- has nothing left to detect.

Do not start this task before .25 is decided. What may survive is much smaller:
a validator asserting the GENERATED file matches its source declaration (a
build-artifact freshness check, the shape .12 already uses for
zz-fallback-binds.conf), rather than a machine-generated ownership map that
parses two independent sources.

The historical regression fixture is still worth keeping either way: run against
the T6-shipped tree (a94dc29) it must report the eight Mod1 collisions. That
fixture is the proof the tooling would have blocked T6.
close_reason: Scope evaporated. This built check --ownership to detect a chord owned by both i3 and binds.py. After the nav cutover (71f6c4a8) they share no chord, and the XI2 measurement showed a shared LAYER chord is harmless by design (daemon shadows i3 while the layer is active, i3 regains it on exit). Nothing left to gate. The historical regression fixture is the part worth keeping -- run against the T6-shipped tree (a94dc29) it should report the eight Mod1 collisions -- re-file that alone if a future migration needs a gate.

title: hotkeyd panic bind: one i3-owned chord resets the keyboard back to i3
design:
User's design call after the T6 revert, recorded in sp020 ## recovery.

The escape hatch as built only ran 'hotkeyd.sh restart'. That helps when the
daemon is DEAD and not at all when it is alive and wrong -- misgrabbing, stuck in
a layer, or serving a table whose chords collide with i3's. Recovery must mean
'give the keyboard back to i3'.

SHAPE
  i3 keeps exactly one bind: $mod+Shift+F12 -> hotkeyd-panic.sh
  panic:  hotkeyd.sh stop  ->  link i3/config.d/zz-fallback-binds.conf into
          ~/.i3/config.d/  ->  i3-msg reload
  resume: remove the link -> reload -> hotkeyd.sh start

No contested-chord window: grabs die with the process and i3 re-takes its own on
reload. Same reasoning that made the T6 revert clean.

REQUIREMENTS, each a real deliverable not a comment:

1. FALLBACK CONTENT = the i3 equivalent of whatever binds.py currently owns.
   NOT "the set i3 owns today" -- an earlier draft of this task said that and it
   is wrong in a way that fails closed. i3 still owns its own binds, so a
   fallback restating them duplicates every one, and i3 treats duplicate
   keybindings as a CONFIG ERROR (nagbar), not last-wins. This repo already
   documents that trap at i3/config.d/native.conf:103. Today binds.py owns only
   $mod+o, so the fallback is $mod+o -> mode "nav" (or empty if $mod+o is
   removed first); after the .16 directional cutover it names that group.
   Freshness test diffs the fallback against binds.py's chord set, NOT against
   i3's.

2. NO OVERRIDE STORY. The zz- prefix settles glob ORDERING only. It does not
   let the fallback shadow a live bind -- see (1). The composed tree must pass
   i3 -C with no duplicate-binding error; that is the check.

3. PANIC CHORD RESERVED UNDER EVERY SPELLING. binds.py's validator refuses any
   table binding it. The validator is display-agnostic while $mod is not, so
   reserving the literal $mod token alone leaves a hole: a table spelling
   Mod1+Shift+F12 steals the chord on :10, Mod4+Shift+F12 on :0. Reserved set is
   Shift+F12 under BOTH modifier resolutions plus the $mod token, normalised.
   One fixture per spelling.

4. PANIC IS MACHINE-WIDE, NOT PER-DISPLAY -- decide and document which.
   ~/.i3/config.d/ is shared: :0 and :10 both include the same glob via
   i3/config (adr0004). So panicking on :10 links a file :0's i3 will parse on
   its NEXT reload, while :0's daemon still holds its grabs -- recreating the
   contested state the ordering argument rules out. Either scope the fallback
   per display, or state plainly that panic is machine-wide and resume must
   precede any reload on the other display. THIS TASK OWNS THE DECISION.

5. TESTS ASSERT REAL OWNERSHIP TRANSFER, not exit codes. Start the daemon,
   confirm it owns a chord, panic, confirm i3 owns that chord again -- read from
   'i3-msg -t get_config' (bindings). NOT get_tree, which returns the window
   tree; an earlier draft of this task said get_tree. Plus the resume
   round-trip, and a case where the daemon is ALIVE AND WRONG (holding a
   colliding grab) rather than merely dead -- that is the state this exists for.

6. test-launcher.sh:108 greps i3/config.common for the literal string
   'hotkeyd.sh restart' and fails if absent. Replacing that bind without
   re-pointing this assertion breaks the suite in the same commit.

WHY IT MATTERS: it converts the blast-radius objection to full migration from a
safety question into a scope question. Worst case becomes one chord away from the
setup that works today -- no terminal, no ssh, no diagnosis needed.

IMMEDIATE CONSUMER: the user wants hotkeyd autostart armed (it has been
commented out in i3/config.d/native.conf:83-84 and wsl.conf:76 since T5). Arming
it while $mod+o is owned by BOTH binds.py:349 and i3/config.common:408 risks the
alive-and-wrong state on an i3 reload. This task is the precondition for that.

Blocks .13 and any resumption of the migration.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED: hotkeyd-panic.sh + zz-fallback-binds.conf + reserved panic chord; escape hatch re-pointed from 'hotkeyd.sh restart' to 'hotkeyd-panic.sh panic'.

Branch bd-dotfiles-hwds.12.0, commit 719a7ef.
Worktree /home/jan/.dotfiles/.claude/worktrees/agent-a3f63945c0118b190

REQUIREMENT 4 DECISION — PANIC IS MACHINE-WIDE, AND ENFORCED NOT DOCUMENTED.
Per-display scoping is unavailable: i3/config is one shared entry point whose
'include ~/.i3/config.d/*.conf' both sessions run, and i3's include takes no
conditionals; a per-display fallback would need a second entry point, i.e. the
hand-synced duplication ft003 deleted. Merely writing 'resume before reloading
the other display' would leave the hazard live and triggerable by a
$mod+Shift+c nobody connects to hotkeyd. So: panic stops the daemon on EVERY
display before linking (so after panic no hotkeyd grabs exist anywhere and any
later reload on any display is safe), and hotkeyd.sh start REFUSES while the
link exists (exit 4), so no autostart/exec_always/xrdp reconnect can rearm one
display behind the fallback. Panic is sticky until resume — the property that
survives a reboot, since the link is on disk and the daemon's absence is not.
Recorded in sp020 ## recovery ('DECIDED (Task 10)'), ft011 ## api_surface, and
the headers of hotkeyd-panic.sh and zz-fallback-binds.conf.

EVIDENCE PER REQUIREMENT
1. FALLBACK CONTENT = binds.py's chords MINUS i3's, not i3's own set.
   i3/config.d/zz-fallback-binds.conf binds NOTHING today: binds.py owns only
   $mod+o and i3/config.common:408 still owns it too. Freshness enforced by
   test_binds.py::test_the_fallback_is_exactly_what_binds_py_owns_and_i3_does_not
   (parametrised Mod4/Mod1) — it diffs against binds.py, not i3.
2. NO OVERRIDE STORY. test-hotkeyd.sh stage 10 runs 'i3 -C' on the composed
   tree (HOME with .i3/config.d + .dotfiles link) for BOTH overlays, with and
   without the fallback linked: 4 PASS, no duplicate-binding error. Stage 10
   also carries a guard-on-the-guard that seeds 'bindsym $mod+o mode nav' and
   asserts i3 -C DOES reject it, so the check is not vacuous.
3. PANIC CHORD RESERVED UNDER EVERY SPELLING. binds.RESERVED_CHORDS =
   {normalize_chord('$mod+Shift+F12', m) for m in ('Mod4','Mod1')}, checked in
   _scan so it covers the global table, layers AND held-modifier sublayers.
   Fixtures: 6 (3 spellings x 2 validator $mod values) + 3 alias forms + 3

title: T6 discovery: qs-focus-border.py's red ring also dies at the nav cutover, not just the bar pill
design:
Found while implementing T6 (dotfiles-zgs4). sp020 Task 7 lists only quickshell/config/Bar.qml as the consumer to cut over, but quickshell/qs-focus-border.py is a SECOND consumer of i3 mode events: COLOR_MODES = {'nav'} (line 38) drives the red focus ring, the standing 'bare letters are WM commands, not input' cue.

The moment T6 deletes mode "nav" from i3/config.common, i3 stops emitting that mode transition and the ring stays teal in nav. So between T6 and T7 a user entering nav gets NO red frame and NO bar pill — nav works, but every visual cue that keys are captured is gone. title: hotkeyd: I3Client trusts inherited I3SOCK — cross-display dispatch and permanent failure after i3 restart
description:
Epic review finding (pre-T6 whole-epic audit). i3_socket_path() (hotkeyd.py:233-238) returns $I3SOCK whenever it is set, and only falls back to 'i3 --get-socketpath' when unset. Two failure modes, both real on this host:

1. CROSS-DISPLAY DISPATCH. i3 exports I3SOCK into the env of every exec'd process. i3/config.d/native.conf:77-78 starts BOTH daemons ('hotkeyd.sh start :0' AND 'start :10') from whichever session's i3 fires the exec_always — and on the native host BOTH the :0 and the :10 xrdp session load native.conf (rotz links one overlay per machine, adr0004 keeps both servers live). So the :10 daemon spawned from :0's i3 inherits :0's I3SOCK, and EVERY dispatch it makes lands on :0's i3: press a daemon-owned chord in the RDP session, a window moves on the native desktop. Which daemon gets which socket is decided by which session's exec_always wins the flock race — nondeterministic. This is live TODAY for the Mod4 chords the daemon already owns on :10 (see the companion bind-table-scope task), and post-T6 it would mis-route the whole nav layer.

2. STALE SOCKET AFTER i3 RESTART. After a full i3 stop/start (new pid, new socket path), the daemon's inherited I3SOCK is stale; I3Client.command()'s two attempts both reconnect to the same dead path and return False forever. The existing test test_client_reconnects_when_i3_restarts (test_daemon.py:315) passes because it injects a lambda path_getter — the production i3_socket_path/I3SOCK precedence is untested.

DESIGN NOTE:
- Never trust inherited I3SOCK. Resolve per-display: run 'i3 --get-socketpath' with env DISPLAY=<the daemon's --display> (subprocess env= argument), which reads the I3_SOCKET_PATH root-window property of the right server. Belt-and-braces: hotkeyd.sh can 'env -u I3SOCK' on spawn, but the daemon-side fix is the load-bearing one (people run hotkeyd.py by hand).
- Re-query the path on every reconnect attempt (already the structure — just make _path_getter return fresh data).
- Tests: (a) I3Client with env I3SOCK pointing at a dead/foreign socket still reaches the fake i3 resolved for its display; (b) keep the existing reconnect test but wire it through i3_socket_path rather than a lambda.

Blocks T6 (dotfiles-zgs4): nav dispatch on :10 must land on :10's i3.

title: hotkeyd: daemon skips table validation at startup and SIGHUP can kill it
description:
Epic review finding (pre-T6 whole-epic audit). AC4 of us019 ('the bind set is validated before it is loaded ... refused rather than silently ignored') is only enforced on the --check path. The daemon itself never calls binds.validate()/load():

1. STARTUP: hotkeyd.py main() -> load_table() (hotkeyd.py:303-317) only checks that BINDS/LAYERS attrs exist. Verified empirically on Xvfb :90: a table with a duplicate chord, an empty command AND a layer with no exit_keys (an un-leavable trap layer) starts fine — 'hotkeyd: 3 chords grabbed'. Post-T6 the escape-hatch restart takes exactly this path, so an invalid binds.py edit + $mod+Shift+F12 loads the broken table silently (duplicates resolve last-wins via LayerEngine._index, trap layers become enterable).

2. SIGHUP: run_daemon's reload guard is 'except Exception' (hotkeyd.py:539), but load_table raises SystemExit (BaseException) for a missing file or missing BINDS/LAYERS attr. design:

Single NotificationServer (bodyMarkup true, image/actions/persistence false, keepOnReload true). Each notif: pipe to qs-notif-store.sh append (body on stdin) + state verb (single-writer). Owns FIFO QS_NOTIF_FIFO 0600, line-wise; dismiss id/latest removes entry + .dismiss() live + rewrites state; garbage ignored. Headless: no Window/PanelWindow. IMPLEMENTED: quickshell/notif/shell.qml (headless daemon, single NotificationServer) + quickshell/test-notif-daemon.sh (22 assertions, 9 named scenarios + SELFTEST).

Evidence:
- Single NotificationServer, flags byte-for-byte replicated (bodyMarkupSupported:true, imageSupported:false, actionsSupported:false, persistenceSupported:false, keepOnReload:true): shell.qml:353-390.
- Two writes per notification, both through qs-notif-store.sh, body on stdin never argv: shell.qml:185-200 (_runNotifyJob), verified via 'notify-lands-in-store'/'state-tracks-count' scenarios (PASS).

- Session-independence (AC1): 'owns-bus-name' scenario starts two daemon instances on one isolated bus, sends one notify-send, asserts exactly one store entry (PASS) -- proves the platform's D-Bus name-singleton, not app logic, but confirms no bar/daemon can double-process.
- No Window/PanelWindow anywhere in shell.qml (grep-verifiable) -- headless service only.
- Edge cases covered by scenarios: critical-flag-cycle (critical 1 on arrival, flips to 0 after dismissing the only critical, PASS), markup-folded-state-raw-store (raw <b> tag survives in store, stripped+newline-folded in state 'last', PASS), burst-10-monotonic (10 notify-send backgrounded <1s, exactly 10 store entries 000001..000010 no gaps, final count 10, PASS), fifo-dismiss-latest re-resolves after a prior dismissal (dismiss latest twice in a row correctly targets 000002 then 000001, PASS).

- Commits: 28b2b29 on bd-dotfiles-c5fd.2.0.
- Deviations:
  1. Added QS_NOTIF_STORE_SCRIPT and QS_NOTIF_READY_FILE env overrides (test-only; production/qs-start.sh never sets them, falls through to the real ~/.dotfiles path). Needed because the daemon otherwise hardcodes $HOME/.dotfiles/quickshell/qs-notif-store.sh (house convention elsewhere in this repo) -- without an override the test suite running from an isolated worktree would invoke a DIFFERENT script than the one under test. QS_NOTIF_READY_FILE gives the test harness a deterministic startup-complete signal (touched after the daemon's startup seq-scan Process completes) instead of guessing QML/D-Bus startup timing.
  2. count/critical semantics: used trackedNotifications.values.length directly (live tracked count) rather than porting the old per-bar 'pending until superseded by ticker' deferred-counting scheme from config/shell.qml's trackCurrent()/dismissLatest(). The old scheme would make burst-10-monotonic's 'final count 10' requirement mathematically impossible (last arrival stays uncounted until superseded or the ticker finishes, giving 9). Confirmed empirically that notify-send -r (replace) never re-fires onNotification and trackedNotifications never double-counts a replace, so this simplification satisfies both the burst-10 and replace-id requirements without extra bookkeeping. Documented in shell.qml:118-127.
  3. state 'last' epoch/text on dismiss/staterefresh writes: preserves the most recent genuine arrival's text/epoch (root._lastEpoch/_lastText) rather than blanking to '' -- the spec doesn't specify this explicitly but blanking on every dismiss seemed like an obvious defect during manual smoke-testing (a dismiss would erase the ticker's last-known text). Discovered via empirical testing (not obvious from the qmltypes API alone): NotificationServer.trackedNotifications.values does NOT update synchronously within the same JS tick as notification.tracked=true or .dismiss() -- a zero-interval Timer tick is required first. Baked into the design as the _afterSettle() mechanism (shell.qml:137-155) rather than discovered later as a flaky-test bug.

Display screen-suffix mismatch: a store path component built from a raw X display carries the screen suffix (:0.0) under a real session, while the autostart launches writers with the bare display (:0). qs-clip.sh (reader) was fixed inline (${DISPLAY%.*} at lines 112, 231). In production they receive bare displays (autostart args / qs-clip already-normalized pass), so no live break — but a manual :0.0 invocation mismatches, and the asymmetry is a latent trap. Root TEST GAP: every suite seeds bare :9x displays, so the writer/reader normalization was never exercised.

title: test-clip-integration.sh: CLIP_FEED_DST is dead after egm.4; feeder falls back to the LIVE clipcat socket
design:
Discovered while doing dotfiles-egm.4 (clip-feed.sh clipcat port). Belongs to
dotfiles-egm.5, whose files_touched already lists i3/scripts/test-clip-integration.sh.

WHAT CHANGED. clip-feed.sh no longer takes a destination DISPLAY. clipcat has no
single well-known socket (one clipcatd binds one socket, and adr0004 gives this
host two displays), so the feeder now takes CLIP_FEED_DST_SOCKET -- an explicit
gRPC socket path -- and falls back to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/clipcat/grpc.sock, or
refuses to start (exit 78) if neither is set.

THE HAZARD. i3/scripts/test-clip-integration.sh:409 still passes the now-dead
CLIP_FEED_DST="$DPY". That variable is simply ignored. The harness isolates
XDG_CONFIG_HOME / XDG_DATA_HOME / XDG_CACHE_HOME but NOT XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, so a
feeder started by that suite silently resolves the fallback -- the LIVE user
sessions clipcat socket. On a machine with a real clipcatd running, that suite
would inject its own fixtures into the users actual clipboard history. Under
copyq this could not happen: the destination was a DISPLAY, and the test drove a
throwaway one.

FIX (for egm.5, alongside its autostart rewrite):
  - set CLIP_FEED_DST_SOCKET to the suites own throwaway socket in i3_exec()
  - add XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$TMP/run" (0700) to the same env block, so even the
    fallback path cannot reach the live session
  - native.conf/wsl.conf must pass --grpc-socket-path to clipcatd and the
    matching CLIP_FEED_DST_SOCKET to clip-feed.sh, per display

NOT FIXED IN egm.4: that file is task 5 scope. egm.4 did not touch it.

design:
### Task 2: qs-clip.sh backend layer — file-store list and set

#### bd

#### type
task

4h

#### depends
Task 6

#### files_touched
`quickshell/qs-clip.sh`, `quickshell/test-clip-history.sh`

#### success_criteria
- `qs-clip.sh list` emits `"<id>\t<preview>"` newest-first (store filename
  seq descending), one line per entry, count equal to the store's entry
  count. Deterministic: two consecutive `list` calls over an unchanged store
  emit byte-identical output.
- Previews are the first non-blank line of the file, truncated to the
  configured width; the full entry is still published intact on `set`.
- `qs-clip.sh set <id>` publishes that entry and propagates `clip-set.sh`'s
  0/1/2 exit verbatim.
- Session derivation unchanged: with two live sessions and no match it still
  refuses and names them rather than guessing.

#### edge_cases
Empty/absent store dir (empty output, exit 0); entry containing tabs,
newlines, or a literal `\n` two-char sequence (preview must not break the
line protocol; `set` must publish raw bytes); unicode previews; an id whose
file vanished between `list` and `set` (exit 1, nothing published); a `.tmp`
file mid-write in the dir (skipped); cap exceeded.

Extend `quickshell/test-clip-history.sh` with file-store fixtures (seeding =
writing files; no daemon). Named scenarios: list-deterministic-two-calls-
identical; list-newest-first-by-seq; preview-is-first-nonblank-line;
tab-in-entry-does-not-break-protocol; literal-backslash-n-vs-real-newline-
distinct (the [[poc012]] case clipcat could not pass);
set-publishes-the-selected-id-not-a-position; stale-id-exits-1-publishes-
nothing; tmp-file-skipped. Mutation: making `set` publish the first id
instead of the selected one must fail; making `list` order by mtime-tie must
not break seq determinism.

title: Callers of clip-paste.sh must pin CLIP_PASTE_DISPLAY
design:
clip-paste.sh (dotfiles-92w.3) refuses to guess when more than one X display has a focused window, which is the permanent steady state on the native host (native i3 :0 + xrdp i3 :10, adr0004; sp014's plan runs copyq on :0 with clip-feed.sh bridging :10 -> :0).

So every caller must pass the session explicitly:

  CLIP_PASTE_DISPLAY="$DISPLAY" clip-paste.sh <row>

title: clip-feed: TOCTOU window between TARGETS gate and payload read can launder a secret
description:
Follow-up from the dotfiles-92w.2 audit (parent epic dotfiles-92w, sp014).

i3/scripts/clip-feed.sh reads TARGETS (line 126) and only then reads the payload
(line 139). Measured gap between the two X SelectionRequests: 10.3 / 13.3 / 11.8 ms
(audit probe, timestamped selection owner). Poll cycle is ~520ms.

If a password-manager copy takes CLIPBOARD ownership INSIDE that gap, the gate has
already passed on the previous (non-secret) owner and read_src fetches the secret
from the NEW owner, feeding it into copyq history. The next poll correctly sees the
hint and skips -- but the secret is already in history. Exposure is roughly
10ms/520ms ~= 2% per password copy on :10.

This is inherent to X: TARGETS and the payload are separate protocol requests and
cannot be fetched atomically. It cannot be eliminated, only narrowed.

Proposed mitigation (cheap, ~3 lines): re-check TARGETS AFTER read_src and BEFORE
feed_dst, and drop the item if the hint is now present. Does not stop the payload
reaching a tmpfile, but does stop it reaching history -- which is the actual harm.

Not a defect in the shipped gate: the gate is correct as designed and was verified
load-bearing during audit (stripping it causes the payload to be fetched; with it
present, 0 payload requests over 16 polls). This is a residual race the task spec
did not cover.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED: post-read TARGETS re-check closes the gate/payload TOCTOU laundering window.

Mitigation (clip-feed.sh:164-173, inside the post-dedup branch):
    if ! targets || grep -qFx 'application/x-kde-passwordManagerHint' "$TGT"; then
      nap "$POLL"; continue
    fi
Reuses the existing timeout-wrapped targets() helper, so no new xclip call and
no new bare-DISPLAY call. Fails CLOSED (a re-check that times out or finds no
owner also drops). $LAST is deliberately NOT updated, so a legitimate copy
dropped because an owner hung is simply re-fed on the next poll -- self-healing.
Costs one extra TARGETS round-trip per DISTINCT new item, not per poll.

Evidence:
- Race exercised for real, not asserted structurally: new race-owner.py fixture
  owns CLIPBOARD with a benign hint-free window, then hands the selection to a
  hint-bearing window from INSIDE the handler for the feeder's own TARGETS
  request (after the SelectionNotify is flushed). The feeder's next request --
  the payload read -- is answered by the password-manager owner. Gate passed on
  win1, payload came from win2. Deterministic, fired in 3/3 runs.
- Each race scenario asserts the handoff actually fired ('handed' in owner.out)
  BEFORE asserting no leak, so a scenario that silently degraded into an
  ordinary benign copy cannot produce a vacuous green.
- RED (pre-fix, committed at fe116ef): 'toctou-race' FAILED -- history 4->5,
  cq read 0 == RACE-SECRET-marker, 'raced secret appears in no history row'
  reported 'row 0'. The reported vulnerability reproduced end-to-end.
- GREEN (post-fix): 35 passed / 0 failed, three consecutive runs.
- MUTATION CONTROL 'CONTROL recheck-is-load-bearing': strips ONLY the re-check
  (first gate left intact), reruns the same race -> 'raced secret IS fed when
  the re-check is absent', size before+1, cq read 0 == RACE-SECRET-CONTROL.
  Both halves present.
- awk strip ranges verified by diff: each removes exactly its own block and
  nothing else; all three variants pass sh -n.

Interaction found and handled (would have silently degraded an existing test):
the pre-existing 'CONTROL hint-check-is-load-bearing' stripped only the first
gate -- with the re-check added, the re-check would have caught that copy and
the control would have started asserting nothing while still printing PASS.
It now strips BOTH checks (they are defence in depth against the same hint) and
says so in a comment. To stop the first gate losing coverage, clip-owner.py now
logs each payload SelectionRequest and 'secret-not-laundered' asserts the first
gate's STRONGER unique property: the payload is never even REQUESTED, so it
never touches a tmpfile -- something the post-read re-check cannot provide.

Residual exposure (documented in the clip-feed.sh header, not hidden):
1. The secret payload DOES reach $NEW (mktemp, 0600, /tmp) before being
   dropped. On disk for one poll. Unavoidable without atomic TARGETS+payload
   fetch, which X does not provide. Accepted per the issue.
2. Narrowed, not eliminated: a THIRD owner taking CLIPBOARD between the payload
   read and the re-check would present hint-free targets and the secret would be
   fed. Requires two ownership flips inside ~10ms; the single-flip case the
   feeder is actually exposed to is covered.
3. Only hint-publishing password managers are recognised at all. One that
   advertises no hint is indistinguishable from a normal copy at BOTH checks.

Tests: i3/scripts/test-clip-feed.sh, 27 -> 35 assertions, all green.
Commits on bd-dotfiles-l6s.0: fe116ef (RED test), 8c82b7e (fix + controls).
Deviations: none from the proposed mitigation. Env: xorg-server-xvfb is not
installed (dotfiles-saa); extracted the pacman package to scratch and ran with
XVFB= override, which the suite already honours.
close_reason:
AUDITED: APPROVED (reviewer reproduced RED, GREEN, and both mutation controls independently)

CONTRACT: re-check TARGETS after read_src, before feed_dst; drop if hint present.
Implemented at clip-feed.sh:171-173, inside the post-dedup branch, reusing the
existing timeout-wrapped targets() helper. No deviation from the proposed fix.

THE RACE IS GENUINELY EXERCISED (the crux -- verified, not accepted):
The strongest evidence is the mutation control's own output, which needs no
trust in the fixture's self-reporting. 'CONTROL recheck-is-load-bearing' strips
ONLY the re-check, leaving the FIRST gate intact, and the run feeds
RACE-SECRET-CONTROL (win2's hint-bearing payload) into history at row 0.
With the first gate intact, that outcome is only reachable if the gate passed
on win1 (hint-free) while the payload was answered by win2 (hint-bearing).
That IS the TOCTOU race, demonstrated by outcome rather than asserted.
Reviewer confirmed the strip guards: the awk range removes exactly the re-check
(FATAL if 'SECURITY GATE' is lost too), and all variants pass sh -n.

RED reproduced by reviewer: new test file + main's pre-fix clip-feed.sh ->
exit 1, 30 passed / 5 failed. 'toctou-race': history 4 -> 5, 'newest item'
actual RACE-SECRET-marker, 'raced secret appears in no history row' -> row 0,
plus 2 cascade failures in later scenarios seeing the leaked row. The reported
vulnerability reproduces end-to-end against the shipped feeder.

GREEN reproduced by reviewer: 35 passed / 0 failed, exit 0, three consecutive
runs (:88/:87). 'the handoff fired' PASSed in both race scenarios in all three
runs -- deterministic, no flake.

FIRST GATE HAS NOT LOST COVERAGE (the implementer's self-reported near-miss,
verified repaired). Adding the re-check would have hollowed out the existing
'CONTROL hint-check-is-load-bearing' -- it stripped only the first gate, so the
re-check would have caught the copy and the control would have printed PASS
while asserting nothing. Repair verified two ways:
 a) the control now strips BOTH blocks (test-clip-feed.sh:514-521) with a FATAL
    guard that the hint string is gone; it passes only by actually feeding.
 b) 'secret-not-laundered' now asserts the first gate's STRONGER unique
    property -- the payload is never even REQUESTED. Reviewer proved this
    assertion is NON-vacuous by mutation: a mutant with the first gate stripped
    and the re-check intact flips it to FAIL / actual 'requested', while
    'secret text appears in no history row' still PASSes. The two gates are
    therefore demonstrably distinct in strength, not redundant.

FAIL-CLOSED + NO SILENT DATA LOSS (verified by reading clip-feed.sh:171-174):
'! targets ||' means a re-check that times out (timeout -> nonzero) or finds no
owner (xclip -> nonzero) also drops. $LAST is updated only at line 174,
'feed_dst && cp "$NEW" "$LAST"', reachable only after the re-check passes --
so a legitimate copy dropped by a transient hang is re-fed next poll rather
than lost. The 35-test green run (which includes every ordinary capture,
dedup, src-down/return and cold-start scenario) confirms the re-check does not
eat legitimate clipboard content.

SP014 HARD REJECTS HOLD: '#!/bin/sh' (line 1) + 'set -u' (line 73); both xclip
call sites (109, 134) are timeout-wrapped with an explicit DISPLAY=; no bare
'xclip -o'; the re-check reuses targets() so it adds no new call site and no
bare-DISPLAY path. Suite still launches the feeder with DISPLAY=:77 (bogus).

RESIDUAL EXPOSURES -- accurately characterized in the header (49-61), neither
overstated nor hidden:
 1. payload reaches $NEW before the drop -- CONFIRMED empirically by the
    mutation above ('requested'); unavoidable without atomic TARGETS+payload
    fetch, which X does not provide. Explicitly accepted by the issue.
 2. two-flip race still leaks -- accurate reading of the code; needs two
    ownership changes inside ~10ms.
 3. non-hint-publishing managers unprotected -- accurate; both checks grep the
    same hint string.
None is cheaply fixable inside this contract. Filed dotfiles-d6k (P3) for the
one additive hardening found: truncate $NEW on the drop path to cut the
secret's on-disk lifetime from one poll to microseconds.

AUTOMATED CHECKS: no TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK/STUB in either file; sh -n and bash -n
clean; no dead code; no fallback/compat shims.

SCOPE: exactly i3/scripts/clip-feed.sh + i3/scripts/test-clip-feed.sh.
Zero quickshell paths touched (sibling agent on task .4 unaffected).
Branch merges cleanly onto main (102e45a).

Tests: 35 passed / 0 failed (27 -> 35, 8 new). Deviations: none.

#### edge_cases

#### test_plan

notes:
REVIEW FIX: orphaned sleep-3600 leak in fake preview-wv stub (reviewer-caught gap).

Root cause: the stub's TERM trap did `exit 0` without killing its
backgrounded `sleep 3600` child (nushell/actions/preview-test:139
formerly `trap 'exit 0' TERM`). Every wrapper-initiated SIGTERM (window
--close, stop) killed the outer script but orphaned the sleep to PID 1 for
up to an hour. 5 leaks per suite run (tests 10, 12, 13, 17x2) — reviewer's
ps showed 20 PPID-1 orphans across 4 batches. Confirmed independently: my
own ps -eo pid,ppid,etimes,cmd | grep 'sleep 3600' showed the same 20
orphans (etimes 198-407s, matching my 2 preceding runs + reviewer's 2)
before the fix — my earlier 'no leftover processes' claim was wrong; I'd
only checked stub *scripts* (pgrep -f preview-wv) and the daemon, not the
stub's own detached sleep grandchild.

Fix: trap changed to `trap 'kill $! 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM` — $! is
the most recently backgrounded job (the sleep), killed before the script
exits. No-exec design preserved (tracked pid's /proc/<pid>/cmdline still
reads the script's own args, so cmdline-verification tests are unaffected).

Deviations from design (both necessary, not scope creep — same file set: preview-webview/src/main.rs, preview-webview/Cargo.toml):
1. Added gtk/glib/gdkx11/x11 as explicit direct deps (matching tao 0.30's internal gtk-rs 0.18 versions) to call gtk::init() ourselves before tao::EventLoop::new(). tao's own EventLoop::new() calls gtk_init internally via .expect(), which PANICS with a backtrace when DISPLAY is unset/unreachable — violates the 'no DISPLAY -> clean error, no panic' edge case.   silently.

title: T7: akm/d2 iframe embed + lazy-spawn
design: See sp008 ### Task 7 for full H4 props.
notes:
DEVIATION 1: server.go touched (not in files_touched: proxy.go, render.go, static/shell.html) — added mux.HandleFunc("/d2embed/", s.handleD2Embed) registration + two special-case dispatch blocks in handleFile (isD2Ext/isAkmZettel, before the renderFile call), mirroring the EXACT precedent already set by Task 8's ?live special-case in the same function (flagged there as a deviation too). Needed because renderD2Embed requires reqPath and renderAkmEmbed requires s.root, neither available inside renderFile's existing signature.

DEVIATION 2: static/shell.html NOT modified. Investigated whether the outer shell iframe (#content) needs changes to support nested/embedded content — it has no sandbox attribute restricting nested iframes, so /file/<path> returning HTML with its own embedded <iframe> (akm) or the d2embed proxy target works unchanged. No concrete requirement found; left as-is.

DESIGN NOTE (poc006-driven split, per task's own guidance to read poc006 for the exact shape): akm zettels get a genuine cross-origin <iframe src="http://127.0.0.1:<akm-graph-port>/"> (poc006 confirmed zero frame-blocking headers -> safe, no proxy needed). .d2 files instead get an <iframe src="/d2embed/<path>"> pointing at a NEW same-origin route (handleD2Embed in proxy.go) that resolves the file via d2-router's GET /api/resolve, then reverse-proxies that ONE page response with X-Frame-Options/CSP-frame-ancestors stripped (proxyAndStripFrameHeaders) — this is the only way 'the proxy strips it' (success criteria) is achievable, since a genuinely cross-origin iframe gives preview-d zero visibility into the upstream response headers.

Lazy-spawn: ensureDaemonRunning(mu, port, spawnFunc) does double-checked-locking health-probe -> lock -> re-probe -> spawn -> bounded poll-wait (daemonSpawnWait=10s, daemonSpawnPoll=150ms, both overridable package vars for fast tests). akmGraphSpawn/d2RouterSpawn are package-level func vars (test seam, spied in tests) wrapping spawnDaemonBinary (exec.LookPath check -> exec.Command().Start() -> background Wait() to reap, avoiding zombies). Concurrency-race-tested with -race and 8 concurrent goroutines (TestEnsureDaemonRunningConcurrentCallersSpawnOnce, TestHandleFileAkmZettelLazySpawnsSingleDaemonUnderConcurrency) -- single spawn confirmed.

All new + existing preview/ tests pass under go test ./... -race (no regressions).
close_reason:
AUDITED: APPROVED

Criteria verified:
- Cross-origin akm iframe: TestHandleFileAkmZettelEmbedsCrossOriginIframe passes; render.go renderAkmEmbed / proxy.go:319-325 emits <iframe src="http://127.0.0.1:<port>/"> direct to akm-graph, no proxy (poc006-consistent: akm-graph emits zero frame-blocking headers).
- d2 same-origin proxy embed: TestHandleFileD2FileEmbedsViaD2EmbedRoute passes; proxy.go:334-341 renderD2Embed emits <iframe src="/d2embed/<path>">, proxy.go:369-398 handleD2Embed resolves via d2-router's /api/resolve then proxies.
- Lazy-spawn: TestEnsureDaemonRunningSpawnsWhenDown, TestHandleFileAkmZettelLazySpawnsSingleDaemonUnderConcurrency pass — spawn fires exactly once when daemon down.
- Spawn-race single-spawn under concurrency: TestEnsureDaemonRunningConcurrentCallersSpawnOnce (8 goroutines) and TestHandleFileAkmZettelLazySpawnsSingleDaemonUnderConcurrency (5 goroutines) both assert spawnCalls==1; verified PASS under `go test -race -count=1` (ran independently, not just trusting report). ensureDaemonRunning (proxy.go:156-176) uses real double-checked locking: probe -> mu.Lock -> re-probe -> spawn -> bounded poll, mutex genuinely guards the check-spawn-wait sequence.
- Header-strip is real, not tautological: TestProxyAndStripFrameHeadersRemovesXFrameOptions sends a real upstream X-Frame-Options:DENY + CSP frame-ancestors via httptest.Server and asserts both are absent from the proxied response while body/other headers pass through (TestProxyAndStripFrameHeadersPassesThroughOtherHeaders). End-to-end through the real /d2embed/ route in TestHandleD2EmbedProxiesResolvedURLAndStripsFrameHeaders (3-hop: client -> preview-d -> stub d2-router -> stub d2 page emitting XFO:DENY).
- Backend-unavailable graceful (both akm + d2): TestHandleFileAkmZettelBackendUnavailableWhenSpawnFails, TestHandleFileD2BackendUnavailableWhenSpawnFails — spawn failure -> 200 HTML with 'unavailable' marker, no <iframe>, never a 500/hang.
- Health-wait bounded timeout: TestEnsureDaemonRunningTimesOutWhenNeverHealthy — spawn 'succeeds' but daemon never binds; verified elapsed >= daemonSpawnWait and < 2x via -race run (0.31s using shortened test budget). TestEnsureDaemonRunningSpawnErrorReturnsWithoutWaiting proves a spawn error short-circuits without paying the health-wait.
- Path-jail on /d2embed/ (new attack surface): handleD2Embed (proxy.go:369-385) calls resolveInRoot(s.root, reqPath) BEFORE any network I/O to d2-router — same containment check (syntactic + symlink, path.go:36-71) as /file/<path> and /open. TestHandleD2EmbedOutOfRootRejected proves ../../etc/passwd -> 400. No SSRF: the only value proxied is d2-router's own /api/resolve response for an already-validated in-root absolute path; d2-router is the same trusted no-auth localhost daemon ft002 already is (consistent threat model, not a new trust boundary).
- server.go deviation: additive only — two new dispatch blocks in handleFile (isD2Ext/isAkmZettel checks before renderFile call, server.go:361-368) mirroring Task 8's already-precedented ?live special-case immediately above; mux.HandleFunc(\"/d2embed/\", ...) registered in its own block (server.go:97-100). No existing routes/dispatch altered. Diff confirms only 5 files touched (proxy.go, proxy_test.go, render.go, render_test.go, server.go) + spec doc, matching declared+logged-deviation scope.

title: [bug] clip-sync wedges on blocking xclip -o (no timeout) — image selection owner hangs the loop
description: clip-sync.sh calls 'xclip -selection <sel> -o' with no timeout. Under xrdp/WSLg, if the selection owner is unresponsive (e.g. an image/bmp selection, or a dead xrdp client), xclip -o blocks indefinitely. One hung read freezes the whole poll loop -> PRIMARY<->CLIPBOARD sync stops -> paste serves stale content. Observed: daemon child 'xclip -selection clipboard -o' stuck 1m34s, a separate 'xclip -selection clipboard -t image/bmp -o' stuck 2h. Fix: wrap all xclip invocations in 'timeout' so a hung read/write is abandoned and the loop continues next tick. Follow-up to dotfiles-m1y / dotfiles-f3c.
close_reason: timeout-guarded all xclip calls; live-tested both directions, no wedge

title: [bug] clip-sync autostart pkill self-matches launcher — daemon never survives i3 reload
description: wsl.conf line 24 'pkill -f i3/scripts/clip-sync.sh; ~/.i3/scripts/clip-sync.sh &' runs via sh -c. The sh -c cmdline contains the substring 'i3/scripts/clip-sync.sh', so pkill -f matches its own parent shell + the just-launched child, killing clip-sync before it runs. Result: no PRIMARY<->CLIPBOARD sync in WSL/xrdp, only a stale orphan xclip -i. Regression in dotfiles-f3c (commit 88d862d). Fix: anchor pkill pattern with $ so it matches the running script cmdline (ends in clip-sync.sh) but not the launcher (ends in &).

title: bd git auto-hooks installed despite akm bd init — stale jsonl import clobbers closes during work-merge
description: Found during work-merge of dotfiles-ak8.1 (branch bd-dotfiles-ak8.1.1, merge 5f88717). /home/jan/.dotfiles/.git/hooks contains post-checkout and post-merge bd hooks. During land-bd-task.sh (git checkout main + git merge), the hooks re-imported the stale .beads jsonl snapshot and reverted dotfiles-ak8.1 from CLOSED back to OPEN/P2, wiping the audit-evidence close and the implementer notes. The close had to be re-applied manually. CLAUDE.md states 'bd auto-hooks are uninstalled by akm bd init' and config.yaml has no-auto-flush/no-auto-import — but the hooks are present, so something re-installed them (bd hooks install?). Fix: re-run akm bd init (idempotent per CLAUDE.md) and find what re-installs the hooks, or the clobber loop will eat every reviewer close that coincides with a git checkout/merge.
close_reason:
Remediated — verified 2026-07-20, no code change needed. The acute clobber cannot occur in the current state.

The bug (2026-06-12): active post-checkout/post-merge bd hooks ran bd import on every git checkout/merge, reloading the stale jsonl and reverting closed issues to open.

Current state, verified:
- Every bd hook in .git/hooks is an INERT worktree-guard stub — no bd import/export/hooks-run logic in any of them (grep-confirmed). post-checkout/post-merge do not exist as active hooks; bd hooks list reports both 'not installed'.
- akm bd doctor --diagnose: all green, incl. '✓ no auto-export/import hook logic', export.auto=false, dolt.auto-commit=on, snapshot in sync with Dolt.
- Ran akm bd init (the issue's own prescribed idempotent remedy) to re-assert: 'bd auto-hooks stripped, bd config pinned, Dolt schema healed'. Removed two dead post-*.disabled leftover files from .git/hooks.

Reinstaller identified (the issue's open question 'find what re-installs the hooks'): NOT anything in the dotfiles automation (grep of *.sh/*.nu/akm found no 'bd hooks install'). It is a MANUAL 'bd hooks install' — bd's own 'bd doctor' nags 'Missing 2 recommended hooks'. Verified in an isolated throwaway repo that bd 1.0.4's 'bd hooks install' writes hooks running 'bd hooks run post-merge/post-checkout' (clobber-capable; an explicit 'bd hooks run' is NOT stopped by the no-auto-import config guard).

Recurrence is self-defended: akm's bd_race_hooks regex 'bd +(export|import|hooks +run)' MATCHES a reinstalled 'bd hooks run' hook, so akm bd doctor detects + strips it, and CLAUDE.md documents 'run akm bd init after bd hooks install re-installs auto-hooks'. The akm hardening (bd_race_hooks treating inert worktree-gate stubs as harmless; bd_strip_hooks) clearly landed after this June-12 issue and is what produced the current safe state.

Durable hardening (core.hooksPath redirect to permanently defeat bd hooks install) was considered and declined as disproportionate: acute bug remediated, recurrence needs a manual mis-step against documented guidance, and akm bd doctor already auto-heals it. Filed nothing further.
